Lately, I've been doing some reflecting on my grandfather, President John F. Kennedy, and his legacy of hope.
In my run to fight for NY-12 in Congress, and just as a person, that's what I want to focus on. Hope.
My name is Jack, or John Bouvier Kennedy Schlossberg if you want to know the whole thing.
In high school, I spent hours watching my grandfather's speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. When we fight for hope, we're not just doing it for ourselves, we're doing it for each other and the future we all have to share.
I know I have big shoes to fill. In my grandfather's memory, I've led a life of caring about this a lot. I put that care and effort and hope into everything I do.
But this is bigger than me. It's bigger than my family's legacy.
Hope is hard to find in Politics these days, but if we let it die out completely, that's how we really lose. Now cannot be the time to stop caring or turn away. We have to double down in our pursuit of hope.
I really think this election is the one — our last chance to stop Trump and change the direction we're heading in.
I need you to know that I believe we can do it. I believe in hope, and I believe in us. Will you believe with me? name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: Sunday News Digest: 3/8/2026
body:
Election questions, the Holt case, and why major companies are leaving the state.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**March 8, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
This week at Rocky Mountain Voice, one theme kept surfacing again and again: **trust.**
Trust in our elections. Trust in our institutions. And trust that Colorado is still a place where people can speak up, ask questions and build businesses without paying a price for it.
One of the most compelling stories this week comes out of the Pikes Peak region, where former fire chief Erik Holt is appealing his case in federal court after he says he was [fired weeks after reporting election irregularities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). His case raises a fundamental question: what happens when public employees believe they’ve seen something wrong in the election system? Can they safely report it—or do they risk their careers?
We’ll be following Holt’s case closely, and later this month, pending approval, we plan to livestream the oral arguments on March 17.
Meanwhile, the debate around Colorado’s elections continues to intensify.
Former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters remains in prison as her attorneys ask Polis to [grant clemency](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), pointing to a [stark sentencing contrast with former state senator Sonya Jaquez Lewis](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), who was convicted under the [same statute](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) for attempting to influence a public servant but received probation rather than prison time.
And a newly filed complaint under the federal Help America Vote Act is raising another set of questions—this time about Colorado’s voter database. Researchers reviewing publicly available voter files say nearly [487,000 voter participation records changed after elections were already certified](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) across the 2020, 2022 and 2024 cycles. The complaint does not allege fraud, but it does argue voters deserve clear answers about why official records continue changing after certification.
But elections weren’t the only issue raising concerns this week. Colorado’s business climate is also facing [new scrutiny after several high-profile corporate moves](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) raised questions about whether the state’s regulatory environment is pushing companies elsewhere, and if we're [following California's risky fiscal road](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
The [most visible example is Palantir](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), the largest publicly traded company once headquartered in Colorado. In February, the tech firm quietly announced it was relocating its headquarters to Miami—no press conference, just a single sentence posted online (after [protests outside their office](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by Dem lawmakers... also, a [new AI law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that could have something to do with it). Analysts estimate the move could [pull roughly $48.6 million in annual compensation out of Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and ripple into hundreds of lost jobs and more than $100 million in economic output statewide.
When businesses leave, they don’t just move an office address. They take jobs, tax revenue and economic momentum with them. And when voters begin to question the transparency of elections, the consequences ripple even further.

# [This Lady Wants to Make History and FLIP THIS SEAT!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/03/08/this-lady-wants-to-make-history-and-flip-this-seat/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)

By **Elizabeth Farnham** on March 8, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 03.08.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=01da14adb81c786f11a5775013ab607edb0d9e5d390c4813ee8276372606d1fd&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6498&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=d2989cdbccf5ec4312371bf7677f375f&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=706db5e52eb2376d2c2169e1b359a8e9)**

| | |
---
Happy Women’s History Month!
---
This nation would not be the world superpower it is without the countless contributions from women. We are half of the population and deserve EQUAL RIGHTS. It is atrocious that a woman’s paycheck, rights over her own body, and representation in leadership are not equal to those of a man from state to state. I run so that we can have agency over our own body, earn equal pay for equal work, and have real representation in our federal government.
---
Together, we CHOOSE DEMOCRACY!
---
| | | |
---
Many thanks to Roger Lund for graciously opening his home to his neighbors so they could sign my petition and hear me speak. It was a delightful afternoon of important conversation and delicious chocolate!
---
If you would like me to speak to you and your neighbors and/or friends and family in your home, please email me at **bethfarnhamforcongress@gmail.com.** I’d be glad to speak and answer questions you have about my positions on the issues and our 13th Congressional District. I’ll even bring literature and yards signs.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=b25828203de7bc243ae50a7d1301ade8a6fa4cc016b068eecc8ad7331863387e&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6498&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=ee8fda917d4970e056b4eeacf550fc91&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=706db5e52eb2376d2c2169e1b359a8e9)

| **What a Performance in Adams County!**
---
DO YOU HEAR THE PEOPLE SING?
---
...THEN JOIN IN THE FIGHT THAT WILL GIVE YOU THE RIGHT TO BE FREE!!!
---
I was blessed to attend the FANTASTIC performance of Les Misérables by students at New Oxford High School tonight.
---
Perhaps it was just a form of entertainment for some, but for me, it was the right message at the right time, delivered exceptionally well by local performers and crew.
---
Some people ask, “Why do we need government services like SNAP food assistance, Medicaid, affordable housing, or even the Environmental Protection Agency?”
---
The answer can be found in a thrilling musical based on a novel by Victor Hugo from the 19th century.
---
Because we don’t want our fellow citizens to live in grinding poverty, compelled to:
– drink tainted water,
– exchange sexual favors for money,
– send their kids away for forced labor,
– die of preventable diseases,
– suffer a 19 year sentence for stealing a loaf of bread,
– be so hungry they steal a loaf of bread in the first place,
– or be exploited and humiliated in any other way by a wealthy ruling class.
---
Representatives who vote in the best interests of Everyday Americans are necessary so that we aren’t at the mercy of such dire straits or odious ultra-wealthy people.
---
As our elected US Representative, I pledge to:
– undo the harm of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act which reduced the necessary benefits of food assistance and healthcare based on a tremendous exaggeration of fraud,
– strengthen our social safety nets like Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security, WIC, and affordable housing,
– ensure that the Ultra-wealthy pay their fair share in taxes,
– re-establish the power of the EPA,
– increase the federal minimum wage from one of poverty to a livable one,
– install a national healthcare plan,
-and MORE!
---
And when we have the rights and benefits that support our human dignity especially in our time of greatest need, then we ARE FREE!
---
Please vote for me in the May Primary election and the November General election.
---
Together, we [**#ChooseDemocracy**](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=1c03768db70d68de7c37af1912c74c44c99b97b87fd96a92e67a5f7b97d3a9fd&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6498&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=7b269499b475f61c9d091598428eb59a&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cudGlrdG9rLmNvbS90YWcvY2hvb3NlZGVtb2NyYWN5&email_id=706db5e52eb2376d2c2169e1b359a8e9) and Liberty!

| **Discussing Food Assistance Changes in Cumberland County**
---
Many thanks to the Cumberland County Food Safety Alliance for their excellent program at Dickenson College on “Navigating Changes in Food Assistance”. Zack Zook and Caryn Long Earl provided solid information about current trends in the community and attempts by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to try to meet the needs of the people.
---
While it’s no surprise that H.R. 1, a.k.a. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, reduces food assistance to hungry Americans and healthcare to those in need, the breadth of its impact right here in South Central Pennsylvania is still staggering.
---
Already, thousands of hungry residents of Cumberland County have attrited from the SNAP program, not because they have less need, but because new work requirements are not within their control, access to the Internet to update information is difficult to come by, and concern about masked agents of the state kidnapping the parents of those citizens who qualify for the benefits are taking their toll. It is outrageous that the richest nation in the world still fails to feed its citizens adequately.
---
Many thanks to the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture for their new websites and funding to try to make things easier for hungry Pennsylvanians.
---
I am fighting to be elected so we can stop providing tax breaks for billionaires at the expense of empty stomachs.
---
Please vote for me on November 3rd so I can work with other caring members of Congress to stamp out hunger.
---

As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you... | | | | | or ---|---|--- By Elizabeth Farnham on March 8, 2026 | District Round-up 03.08.26 Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here: | | | Happy Women’s History Month! This nation would not be the world superpower it is without the countless contributions from women. We are half of the population and deserve EQUAL RIGHTS. It is atrocious that a woman’s paycheck, rights over her own body, and representation in leadership are not equal to those of a man from state to state. I run so that we can have agency over our own body, earn equal pay for equal work, and have real representation in our federal government. Together, we CHOOSE DEMOCRACY! | | | | Many thanks to Roger Lund for graciously opening his home to his neighbors so they could sign my petition and hear me speak. It was a delightful afternoon of important conversation and delicious chocolate! If you would like me to speak to you and your neighbors and/or friends and family in your home, please email me at bethfarnhamforcongress@gmail.com. I’d be glad to speak and answer questions you have about my positions on the issues and our 13th Congressional District. I’ll even bring literature and yards signs. Together, we Photo credit: Jack Stansbury | What a Performance in Adams County! DO YOU HEAR THE PEOPLE SING? ...THEN JOIN IN THE FIGHT THAT WILL GIVE YOU THE RIGHT TO BE FREE!!! I was blessed to attend the FANTASTIC performance of Les Misérables by students at New Oxford High School tonight. Perhaps it was just a form of entertainment for some, but for me, it was the right message at the right time, delivered exceptionally well by local performers and crew. Some people ask, “Why do we need government services like SNAP food assistance, Medicaid, affordable housing, or even the Environmental Protection Agency?” The answer can be found in a thrilling musical based on a novel by Victor Hugo from the 19th century. Because we don’t want our fellow citizens to live in grinding poverty, compelled to: – drink tainted water, – exchange sexual favors for money, – send their kids away for forced labor, – die of preventable diseases, – suffer a 19 year sentence for stealing a loaf of bread, – be so hungry they steal a loaf of bread in the first place, – or be exploited and humiliated in any other way by a wealthy ruling class. Representatives who vote in the best interests of Everyday Americans are necessary so that we aren’t at the mercy of such dire straits or odious ultra-wealthy people. As our elected US Representative, I pledge to: – undo the harm of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act which reduced the necessary benefits of food assistance and healthcare based on a tremendous exaggeration of fraud, – strengthen our social safety nets like Medicaid, SNAP, Social Security, WIC, and affordable housing, – ensure that the Ultra-wealthy pay their fair share in taxes, – re-establish the power of the EPA, – increase the federal minimum wage from one of poverty to a livable one, – install a national healthcare plan, -and MORE! And when we have the rights and benefits that support our human dignity especially in our time of greatest need, then we ARE FREE! Please vote for me in the May Primary election and the November General election. Together, we and Liberty! PS. This clip is a reprise of the grand finale which we were allowed to record since it also included former cast members from the 2016 performance. | | | An Exciting Petition Signing in Cambria County Did you guess former US Representative Connor Lamb from last week’s District Round-up? He was the speaker who used my microphone after I addressed the wonderful Cambria County Democratic Committee crowd. Many thanks to the CCDC for their great event and to Studio 404 for the terrific space. Connor and I will also be speaking at the No Kings rally in Johnstown on March 28th. Get your signs ready! | | | ---|---|--- Photo credits: Jenn Bentley | Discussing Food Assistance Changes in Cumberland County Many thanks to the Cumberland County Food Safety Alliance for their excellent program at Dickenson College on “Navigating Changes in Food Assistance”. Zack Zook and Caryn Long Earl provided solid information about current trends in the community and attempts by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania to try to meet the needs of the people. While it’s no surprise that H.R. 1, a.k.a. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, reduces food assistance to hungry Americans and healthcare to those in need, the breadth of its impact right here in South Central Pennsylvania is still staggering. Already, thousands of hungry residents of Cumberland County have attrited from the SNAP program, not because they have less need, but because new work requirements are not within their control, access to the Internet to update information is difficult to come by, and concern about masked agents of the state kidnapping the parents of those citizens who qualify for the benefits are taking their toll. It is outrageous that the richest nation in the world still fails to feed its citizens adequately. Many thanks to the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture for their new websites and funding to try to make things easier for hungry Pennsylvanians. I am fighting to be elected so we can stop providing tax breaks for billionaires at the expense of empty stomachs. Dear Hoosier Republicans, No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-ailejd-hhlljjcji-tk/) **_Growth, Security, and Opportunity_** Dear Hoosier Republicans,With the legislative session having concluded, our Hoosier Republicans are walking away with some big wins this session.Republicans kept their focus squarely on lowering costs for Hoosier families. Lawmakers advanced electric utility reforms that expand levelized billing options for vulnerable households and increase consumer flexibility, helping families better manage monthly energy bills. They continued efforts to rein in government waste and improve efficiency, while modernizing policies to reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens and keep Indiana competitive. The goal remains clear: make it easier to live, work, and build a future in Indiana.The General Assembly also moved forward with transformative economic development opportunities, most notably Senate Bill 27 to position Northwest Indiana as the future home of the Chicago Bears. The proposal sets the stage for a major stadium and surrounding development expected to drive construction jobs, private investment, and long-term regional growth. Combined with ongoing business expansions across the state, Republicans are ensuring Indiana remains the Midwest's engine for job creation and capital investment.House Bill 1343 authorizes the Governor to deploy a specially trained Indiana National Guard military police unit statewide when necessary, strengthening emergency response capabilities and coordination with law enforcement. Lawmakers also passed new protections for children online, requiring parental consent and age verification for certain social media users under 16, and approved legislation addressing long-term street camping on public property -- establishing clear standards while prioritizing mental health evaluations, shelter referrals, and diversion. Together, these reforms reinforce a simple commitment: protect Hoosier families, back law enforcement, and keep communities secure.Yours in service, Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman _**Governor Mike Braun Highlights Legislative Wins for Hoosier Families**_ Governor Mike Braun highlighted several accomplishments from the 2026 legislative session, pointing to new policies focused on affordability, job growth, public safety, and education for Hoosier families. Key initiatives included lowering utility costs, strengthening public safety laws, revoking CDLs from individuals without legal status, and giving parents new tools to protect children from harmful social media content."I'm proud of what we accomplished and look forward to continuing our work to make life more affordable for Hoosier families, grow our economy, and keep our communities safe."\- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-r/) _**Governor Mike Braun Honors IU Coach Curt Cignetti with Indiana's Highest Award**_ Governor Mike Braun awarded Curt Cignetti the Sachem Award, Indiana's highest honor, recognizing his leadership and impact following the Hoosiers' undefeated 2025 championship season. Braun also presented the entire Indiana Hoosiers football team with the Sagamore of the Wabash for their historic achievement."Coach Curt Cignetti represented the state of Indiana on the national stage and showed the world that the Hoosier values of grit, perseverance, and hard work are the way to victory." \- Governor Braun via a [press release](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-y/) **2026 State Convention** [Click Here for More Information](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-j/) [Click Here to Individually Register](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-t/) [Click Here to Register as an Organization](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-i/) _**Indiana GOP is Hiring Interns for the Spring & Summer**_ **📱 _News You Can Use_ ** **Governor Mike Braun **[announced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-d/) that Indiana has received a 'AAA' credit rating from Fitch Ratings for the 17th consecutive year, the highest possible rating. Governor Braun said the recognition reflects Indiana's disciplined fiscal management and commitment to responsible management of taxpayer dollars.**Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith** [announced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-h/) the launch of the new "92 and You" initiative, a statewide outreach effort aimed at increasing accessibility and connecting with Hoosiers across Indiana. The initiative will include mobile office hours and town halls beginning this month in several counties, with additional stops to be announced.**Secretary Diego Morales **[welcomed](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-k/) students from Indiana University Southeast to the Secretary of State's Office, where they learned about the office's responsibilities. Morales, an Indiana University alumnus, said it was especially meaningful to host students from the IU community.**Treasurer Daniel Elliott **[joined](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-b/) Elise Nieshalla at the Indiana County Treasurers Association meeting to provide an update on Indiana's financial outlook.**Attorney General Todd Rokita **[urged](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-n/) Hoosiers to remain alert to the signs of human trafficking following recent arrests connected to an alleged sex-trafficking ring in Indianapolis. Rokita emphasized the importance of community awareness in helping law enforcement identify victims and bring traffickers to justice.**Senator Todd Young **[joined](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-p/) bipartisan colleagues to introduce the America's Living Library Act of 2026, legislation aimed at collecting and sequencing genomic data from plants, animals, fungi, and microbes found on U.S. public lands. The effort seeks to create a national biological dataset to support innovation in biotechnology, medicine, agriculture, and national security.**Senator Jim Banks **[delivered](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-x/) the keynote address at the Index of Military Strength event hosted by The Heritage Foundation, discussing the importance of maintaining the world's strongest military and highlighting President Trump's "peace through strength" approach.**Congressman Rudy Yakym **[criticized](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-m/) the Biden-era IRS during a Ways and Means Committee hearing, pointing to nearly $450 million in improper payments sent to ineligible recipients, including nonresident aliens. Yakym said holding the agency accountable for waste, fraud, and abuse is essential to protecting taxpayer dollars.**Congressman Marlin Stutzman **[met](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-c/) with the Indiana Broadcasters Association to discuss the Local Radio Freedom Act, legislation aimed at protecting local radio stations from new taxes, fees, or charges related to public performances. Stutzman said he is proud to cosponsor the bill and support the importance of local broadcasting.**Congressman Jim Baird **[praised](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-q/) the bipartisan passage of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 in the House Agriculture Committee, highlighting provisions that support farmers, agricultural research, and conservation programs. Baird said the bill includes several of his priorities and will help provide long-term stability for farmers in Indiana and across the country.**Congresswoman Victoria Spartz **[introduced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-a/) several bills aimed at lowering costs for farmers and consumers, improving farm equipment safety, and increasing transparency in agricultural programs ahead of the upcoming Farm Bill reauthorization. The legislation focuses on giving farmers the right to repair their equipment, easing certain regulatory burdens, and increasing oversight of commodity checkoff programs.**Congressman Jefferson Shreve **[voted](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-f/) to keep the Department of Homeland Security funded, emphasizing the importance of supporting agencies such as the Coast Guard, TSA, Secret Service, and FEMA to maintain national security and public safety.**Congressman Mark Messmer **[praised](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-z/) the passage of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 in the House Agriculture Committee, highlighting its support for farmers, rural communities, and long-term food security. Messmer said the bill strengthens the farm safety net, invests in conservation and innovation, and helps keep American agriculture competitive.**Congresswoman Erin Houchin** [introduced](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ailejd-hhlljjcji-e/) the Dalilah Law, legislation that would prevent individuals who are not lawfully present in the United States from obtaining commercial driver's licenses and operating commercial trucks. The bill aims to strengthen highway safety following recent crashes involving illegal truck drivers. **_Upcoming Events_****March 12:[Huntington County Lincoln Day Marjorie Taylor Greene shocked the nation when she announced her resignation from Congress.
| Marjorie Taylor Greene shocked the nation when she announced her resignation from Congress.

That resignation has triggered a special election in GA‐14, now set for March 10.

**This district — our district — is suddenly on the brink of deciding more than just one seat._It could determine who controls Congress._**

I’m Shawn Harris. I’m a Democrat. Husband. Father. Retired Brigadier General. Farmer. **And I’m running to represent Northwest Georgia with the seriousness, steadiness, and leadership it’s been missing for years.** [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104437?t=6&akid=23210%2E878179%2EZA6rZq) Make no mistake — **MTG’s resignation is not the end of the chaos she created._Not yet._**

If Republicans hold this seat, they’ll likely elect someone who carries on her legacy: Another extremist. Another conspiracy theorist. Another chaos candidate. Another vote for dangerous, divisive MAGA politics. [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104437?t=7&akid=23210%2E878179%2EZA6rZq) But we — together — have the opportunity to change that.**If we win GA‐14, we don’t just change one district. We send a signal to Congress that the era of chaos is over.**

That’s why I’m writing today: I need you with me, and I need you now.

[We are mobilizing a field program, building a digital operation, and organizing voter outreach — but this special election moves fast, and we need resources immediately. If you can, split a donation between my campaign and the Voter Protection Project. # [Gaza Broke America. Here's How We Recover.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=190312520&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMzEyNTIwLCJpYXQiOjE3NzMwMzk5NzQsImV4cCI6MTc3NTYzMTk3NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.34cHIf4hoO1sOujrElMcNJU-USLiDJ-tLmtNU0515C0)
### What two years of livestreamed atrocity did to our conscience, our politics, and our capacity to feel
| | [Melissa Chaudhry](https://substack.com/@melissa4congress)

There are moments when a nation's failure becomes too large to hide behind slogans.
This is one of them.
For over two years, Americans have watched the destruction of Gaza in real time: children pulled from rubble, parents keening over shrouded bodies, hospitals attacked, neighborhoods erased, hunger used as a weapon, law twisted until it screamed. We have watched this on our phones while making breakfast, while standing in line at the grocery store, while putting our children to bed.
We have watched horror become ambient.
We have watched officials explain the indefensible in the flat voice of bureaucracy. We have watched language itself come under assault: "collateral damage," "restraint," "complexity," "self-defense," words deployed like gauze over an open wound.
And something in America has short-circuited.
Not because people are weak.
Because conscience has limits. And ours has been brutally assaulted, over and over, weaponizing our own humanity against us.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2048efa2-c874-4f0f-b904-ab12677dbbc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is a threshold beyond which repeated exposure to preventable mass suffering, combined with powerlessness to stop it, begins to deform the soul. What has happened to this country is not just polarization. Not just media failure. Not just foreign policy corruption, though it is all of those things.
It is moral injury at scale.
## This did not just happen to Gaza. It happened to us.
Gaza broke something in America.
It broke trust in institutions that still speak the language of human rights while financing and defending atrocity. It broke faith in leaders who ask the public to disbelieve their own eyes. It broke the illusion that if the suffering becomes visible enough, if the facts become undeniable enough, if the children become small enough, then surely the machinery will stop.
It did not stop.
That changes people.
When a person is forced to witness unbearable suffering for a long time, unable to meaningfully intervene, the nervous system does not remain untouched. Compassion can curdle into exhaustion. Grief can harden into rage. Feeling can give way to numbness as a form of self-protection. The will can sag under the repeated lesson that nothing you do matters.
You can only watch a house burn with children inside for so long before something in you either rises, breaks, or goes dark.
America has been living in that condition.
Some people have become obsessive witnesses, unable to turn away because turning away feels like betrayal. Some have gone numb because to feel the full truth every day would shatter their ability to function. Some have retreated into cynicism. Some have clung harder to propaganda because the truth would require too devastating a reckoning. Some have converted helplessness into mockery, tribalism, or bloodlust. Some have simply become tired in the marrow.
These are not random reactions.
They are what happens when conscience is forced to carry more than the political order will allow it to act on.
## A nation can develop a split mind
What happens to a person can happen to a country.
A nation can learn to know and not know. To see and refuse to see. To publicly mourn dead children while funding the weapons that kill them. To praise international law in speeches and hollow it out in practice. To call itself civilized while treating mass suffering as an acceptable price of alliance, profit, or geopolitical convenience.
That is not ordinary hypocrisy.
It is civic dissociation.
The body politic, like the human body, can only endure so much contradiction before it starts sending distorted signals. Grief that is not metabolized becomes numbness, despair, or fury. Pain that is denied does not disappear; it spreads. A conscience forced to witness what it cannot stop begins to flicker. The wires get hot. The fuse blows. The lights remain on, but the moral circuitry is damaged.
That is where we are.
And if we are honest, Gaza did not create this fracture from nothing. It revealed it. It concentrated it. It livestreamed it until denial became obscene.
Because Gaza is not only about Gaza.
It is also about what America has become when empire, bureaucracy, media capture, and partisan cowardice converge. It is about the distance between our national mythology and our actual conduct. It is about a political culture so addicted to managed language that it can watch shredded children and still ask whether the optics are difficult. It is about how thoroughly careerism has colonized conscience.
And millions of people now understand, in their bones, that the system does not reliably respond to moral truth.
That realization is profoundly destabilizing.
## Why this is politically dangerous
A democracy cannot survive forever on procedural theater alone.
It cannot remain healthy when millions of people come to believe that institutions are insulated from suffering, insulated from public will, insulated from truth. It cannot endure when the lesson repeated over and over is that atrocity, once absorbed into the machinery of state interest, becomes normal.
Once people absorb that lesson, they begin to withdraw. Or radicalize. Or dissociate. Or reach for false certainties. Or decide that only force matters, because persuasion, law, and conscience appear to have failed.
This is one of the most dangerous conditions a society can enter: not simply outrage, but learned moral futility.
Because a people who believe nothing works are easier to manipulate. Easier to divide. Easier to brutalize. Easier to govern through exhaustion.
That is why the injury of Gaza is not confined to foreign policy. It has entered the American bloodstream.
You can feel it in the students beaten and smeared for demanding an end to slaughter. You can feel it in the routine dehumanization of Palestinians, Arabs, Muslims, and anyone who refuses to lie politely. You can feel it in the strained conversations at dinner tables, in schools, in sanctuaries, in friendships, in families.
You can feel it in the sinking recognition that many powerful people did not merely fail morally. They would prefer that the rest of us stop noticing.
## But noticing is not the problem
The fact that so many people are heartsick, furious, spiritually exhausted, or disoriented is not proof of weakness.
It is evidence that conscience is still alive.
Pain is often the last honest signal in a dishonest environment.
The problem is not that people feel too much. The problem is that they have been forced to feel so much while being denied meaningful pathways for action, repair, and truth.
So how do we recover?
Not by pretending this did not happen.
Not by lowering the volume of our conscience.
Not by calling numbness maturity.
Not by accepting a politics in which dead children are treated as unfortunate but manageable.
We recover by telling the truth about the injury.
## 1\. Tell the truth plainly
America has been morally injured by what it has enabled, defended, normalized, and forced the public to absorb.
A society cannot participate in, excuse, or accommodate the destruction of a people without damaging itself.
There is no civic innocence available to a nation that funds atrocity and then gaslights its own population about what they are seeing.
Recovery begins with plain speech.
That means refusing euphemism. Refusing sterilized language. Refusing the passive voice that magically evacuates agency from mass death.
A child is not "collateral damage."
A family is not "infrastructure."
Starvation is not "pressure."
Mass death does not become less evil because a spokesperson explains it at a podium.
## 2\. Grieve honestly
A nation that cannot grieve honestly cannot recover honestly.
Not performative grief. Not grief as branding. Real grief.
The kind that slows you down. The kind that makes room for tears, prayer, lamentation, witness, silence. The kind that allows a people to admit that something terrible has happened not only to the victims of violence, but to the moral fabric of everyone made to live alongside it.
Grief is not a distraction from politics.
It is what keeps politics from becoming necrotic.
## 3\. Rebuild the link between conscience and action
Helplessness is corrosive. It hollows out democracy from the inside.
One reason so many people feel psychologically frayed is that they have been trapped in the position of witness without sufficient power. Recovery requires rebuilding the link between conscience and action.
That means organizing, not only feeling.
It means disciplined pressure, not only catharsis.
It means institutions worthy of trust, not only emotional expression.
It means refusing the seduction of despair, because despair is politically convenient for the people who benefit from your paralysis.
Conscience must become organized if it is to remain effective.
That can take many forms: mutual aid, legal advocacy, electoral pressure, media truth-telling, labor action, divestment campaigns, civic education, local coalitions, principled public leadership.
The form will vary.
The principle does not.
Feeling must be given structure or it decays into exhaustion.
## 4\. Recover moral language
One of the deepest injuries of this period has been linguistic.
We have been surrounded by language designed to anesthetize rather than illuminate. We have been asked to treat obvious cruelty as complexity, to treat asymmetry as symmetry, to treat the powerful and the dispossessed as morally interchangeable in a fog of tragic inevitability.
This has not only obscured events.
It has degraded thought.
We need language that can tell the truth cleanly again.
Language that remembers every child is a universe.
Language that refuses to let power hide behind grammar.
Language that knows law is not sacred when severed from justice.
Language that can hold grief without collapsing into sentimentality, and fury without collapsing into dehumanization.
## 5\. Refuse to become what we hate
This is crucial.
There is a temptation, after prolonged exposure to cruelty, to flatten morally. To conclude that only domination is real. To mirror the coldness of the systems one opposes.
But that is not recovery.
That is transmission of injury.
We do not heal conscience by cauterizing it.
The answer to moral numbness is not less humanity. It is deeper, steadier humanity, protected by courage and disciplined by truth.
Mercy is not permissiveness. Compassion is not confusion. Moral clarity does not require abandoning complexity; it requires refusing to use complexity as an alibi for cowardice.
## 6\. Rebuild solidarity
Isolation accelerates despair.
People begin to think they are crazy for feeling what they feel, or alone in feeling it. They begin to mistrust their own perception.
But one of the most hopeful facts of this period is that millions of people, especially young people, did not lose their moral bearings. They saw through propaganda. They refused dehumanization. They recognized Palestinian life as fully human and fully grievable. They stepped forward at personal cost. They kept saying no.
That matters.
Because conscience is contagious too.
Not only numbness. Not only cynicism. Not only fear.
Courage is contagious. Truth is contagious. Refusal is contagious. So is love that has teeth in it.
## What recovery asks of us now
The task now is not merely to denounce what Gaza revealed.
It is to become the kind of people, and build the kind of country, that cannot be made to live alongside such horror without changing course.
A country whose institutions are answerable to human reality.
A political culture that does not require people to sever empathy from citizenship.
A public life in which law, media, and leadership do not function primarily as shock absorbers for empire.
That is a large task.
But large tasks are made of smaller fidelities.
Tell the truth.
Stay human.
Organize your conscience.
Mourn honestly.
Refuse euphemism.
Protect each other from numbness.
Turn witness into structure.
Do not surrender your capacity to feel.
Do not surrender your capacity to act.
Gaza broke America.
But breakage is not the end of the story.
Sometimes what breaks is the lie.
Sometimes what shatters is the illusion that we can remain innocent while other people are crushed in our name.
Sometimes moral fracture is the beginning of moral awakening.
Recovery will not come through forgetting.
It will come through remembrance disciplined into action. Through grief turned outward into solidarity. Through truth spoken so plainly that the machinery can no longer hide behind ceremony. Through ordinary people who refuse to lose their souls just because the powerful have misplaced theirs.
If America is to recover, it will not be because the political class suddenly found its conscience.
It will be because the people refused to surrender theirs.
* * *

The lights remain on, but the moral circuitry is damaged. That is where we are. And if we are honest, Gaza did not create this fracture from nothing. It revealed it. It concentrated it. It livestreamed it until denial became obscene. Because Gaza is not only about Gaza. It is also about what America has become when empire, bureaucracy, media capture, and partisan cowardice converge. It is about the distance between our national mythology and our actual conduct. It is about a political culture so addicted to managed language that it can watch shredded children and still ask whether the optics are difficult. It is about how thoroughly careerism has colonized conscience. And millions of people now understand, in their bones, that the system does not reliably respond to moral truth. That realization is profoundly destabilizing. Why this is politically dangerous A democracy cannot survive forever on procedural theater alone. It cannot remain healthy when millions of people come to believe that institutions are insulated from suffering, insulated from public will, insulated from truth. It cannot endure when the lesson repeated over and over is that atrocity, once absorbed into the machinery of state interest, becomes normal. Once people absorb that lesson, they begin to withdraw. Or radicalize. Or dissociate. Or reach for false certainties. Or decide that only force matters, because persuasion, law, and conscience appear to have failed. This is one of the most dangerous conditions a society can enter: not simply outrage, but learned moral futility. Because a people who believe nothing works are easier to manipulate. Easier to divide. Easier to brutalize. Easier to govern through exhaustion. That is why the injury of Gaza is not confined to foreign policy. It has entered the American bloodstream. You can feel it in the students beaten and smeared for demanding an end to slaughter. You can feel it in the routine dehumanization of Palestinians, Arabs, Muslims, and anyone who refuses to lie politely. You can feel it in the strained conversations at dinner tables, in schools, in sanctuaries, in friendships, in families. You can feel it in the sinking recognition that many powerful people did not merely fail morally. They would prefer that the rest of us stop noticing. But noticing is not the problem The fact that so many people are heartsick, furious, spiritually exhausted, or disoriented is not proof of weakness. It is evidence that conscience is still alive. Pain is often the last honest signal in a dishonest environment. The problem is not that people feel too much. The problem is that they have been forced to feel so much while being denied meaningful pathways for action, repair, and truth. So how do we recover? Not by pretending this did not happen. Not by lowering the volume of our conscience. Not by calling numbness maturity. Not by accepting a politics in which dead children are treated as unfortunate but manageable. We recover by telling the truth about the injury. 1\. Tell the truth plainly America has been morally injured by what it has enabled, defended, normalized, and forced the public to absorb. A society cannot participate in, excuse, or accommodate the destruction of a people without damaging itself. There is no civic innocence available to a nation that funds atrocity and then gaslights its own population about what they are seeing. Recovery begins with plain speech. That means refusing euphemism. Refusing sterilized language. Refusing the passive voice that magically evacuates agency from mass death. A child is not "collateral damage." A family is not "infrastructure." Starvation is not "pressure." Mass death does not become less evil because a spokesperson explains it at a podium. 2\. Grieve honestly A nation that cannot grieve honestly cannot recover honestly. Not performative grief. Not grief as branding. Real grief. The kind that slows you down. The kind that makes room for tears, prayer, lamentation, witness, silence. The kind that allows a people to admit that something terrible has happened not only to the victims of violence, but to the moral fabric of everyone made to live alongside it. Grief is not a distraction from politics. It is what keeps politics from becoming necrotic. 3\. Rebuild the link between conscience and action Helplessness is corrosive. It hollows out democracy from the inside. One reason so many people feel psychologically frayed is that they have been trapped in the position of witness without sufficient power. Recovery requires rebuilding the link between conscience and action. That means organizing, not only feeling. It means disciplined pressure, not only catharsis. It means institutions worthy of trust, not only emotional expression. It means refusing the seduction of despair, because despair is politically convenient for the people who benefit from your paralysis. Conscience must become organized if it is to remain effective. That can take many forms: mutual aid, legal advocacy, electoral pressure, media truth-telling, labor action, divestment campaigns, civic education, local coalitions, principled public leadership. The form will vary. The principle does not. Feeling must be given structure or it decays into exhaustion. 4\. Recover moral language One of the deepest injuries of this period has been linguistic. We have been surrounded by language designed to anesthetize rather than illuminate. We have been asked to treat obvious cruelty as complexity, to treat asymmetry as symmetry, to treat the powerful and the dispossessed as morally interchangeable in a fog of tragic inevitability. This has not only obscured events. It has degraded thought. We need language that can tell the truth cleanly again. Language that remembers every child is a universe. Language that refuses to let power hide behind grammar. Language that knows law is not sacred when severed from justice. Language that can hold grief without collapsing into sentimentality, and fury without collapsing into dehumanization. 5\. Refuse to become what we hate This is crucial. There is a temptation, after prolonged exposure to cruelty, to flatten morally. To conclude that only domination is real. To mirror the coldness of the systems one opposes. But that is not recovery. That is transmission of injury. We do not heal conscience by cauterizing it. The answer to moral numbness is not less humanity. It is deeper, steadier humanity, protected by courage and disciplined by truth. Mercy is not permissiveness. Compassion is not confusion. Moral clarity does not require abandoning complexity; it requires refusing to use complexity as an alibi for cowardice. 6\. Rebuild solidarity Isolation accelerates despair. People begin to think they are crazy for feeling what they feel, or alone in feeling it. They begin to mistrust their own perception. But one of the most hopeful facts of this period is that millions of people, especially young people, did not lose their moral bearings. They saw through propaganda. They refused dehumanization. They recognized Palestinian life as fully human and fully grievable. They stepped forward at personal cost. They kept saying no. That matters. Because conscience is contagious too. Not only numbness. Not only cynicism. Not only fear. Courage is contagious. Truth is contagious. Refusal is contagious. So is love that has teeth in it. What recovery asks of us now The task now is not merely to denounce what Gaza revealed. It is to become the kind of people, and build the kind of country, that cannot be made to live alongside such horror without changing course. A country whose institutions are answerable to human reality. A political culture that does not require people to sever empathy from citizenship. A public life in which law, media, and leadership do not function primarily as shock absorbers for empire. That is a large task. But large tasks are made of smaller fidelities. Tell the truth. Stay human. Organize your conscience. Mourn honestly. Refuse euphemism. Protect each other from numbness. Turn witness into structure. Do not surrender your capacity to feel. Do not surrender your capacity to act. Gaza broke America. But breakage is not the end of the story. Sometimes what breaks is the lie. Sometimes what shatters is the illusion that we can remain innocent while other people are crushed in our name. Sometimes moral fracture is the beginning of moral awakening. Recovery will not come through forgetting. It will come through remembrance disciplined into action. Through grief turned outward into solidarity. Through truth spoken so plainly that the machinery can no longer hide behind ceremony. Through ordinary people who refuse to lose their souls just because the powerful have misplaced theirs. If America is to recover, it will not be because the political class suddenly found its conscience. It will be because the people refused to surrender theirs. If this piece gave language to something you have been carrying, help me keep doing this work. I write to tell the truth plainly, defend human dignity, and build a politics that does not require us to betray our conscience. body:
As promised, Tom Willis is working to bring utility bills down and stop unnecessary price hikes.

# Tom Willis Moves to Stop
# Unfair Electricity Rate Hikes
---
|
---
|
---
| | Dear Friend,

As promised, Tom Willis is working to bring utility bills **down** and stop unnecessary price hikes.
In the West Virginia State Senate this session, Tom passed an amendment to Senate Bill 669 designed to stop unfair electricity rate increases in West Virginia. The amendment prevents utilities from raising rates unless the Public Service Commission can clearly demonstrate that the increase provides a direct benefit to customers.
The measure also requires the commission to publicly explain the math behind any approved rate increase so that West Virginians can see EXACTLY how those decisions are made.
For too long, families across the state have opened their electricity bills wondering why costs continue to rise. Tom believes utilities and regulators should have to prove that increases are justified and beneficial to customers before they take effect.
The amendment is aimed at bringing greater transparency and accountability to the rate-setting process while protecting consumers from unnecessary price hikes.
Tom believes these same principles should be applied nationally. As he campaigns for the U.S. Senate, he is calling for federal policies that prevent predatory behavior by utilities, require transparency from regulators, and ensure consumers are protected from unjustified increases.
West Virginians deserve lower bills and real accountability.
That’s the approach Tom Willis will take to Washington in the U.S. Senate.

## Tesla Sued Over Austin Shooter's Prior Assault
A woman who worked at Tesla's Gigafactory in Austin claims in a lawsuit that the perpetrator of last week's mass shooting at a downtown Austin bar [assaulted her](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu2zAMRb9G3hTQkvNsDR66eHtdOxqUxSRCacmQ6Jfk7wvlF7oQBHhxcHj_fK_fGDmm-2_caZbXLa-JnpVJhMp6j4Wrx_qXxCOz5LMkehf0qwHzpcFqcGvAyO916MLsIbi-o7kfRwvXwRjoHnPvzObJEbjBu9tk0dnJ2qsBfwWayHdxbjCw4PoerB0vYE1w07hNAWj021UNQCFKLhd5kNAL643f-YfKZct7x_ND5KjK_lJmUWapB21Szp3zhtx-aSllFnm1Yz7loT8MTawPrFmZpaWUWZqGMgvYNtqGZ5WY9P1MOyadcKegY9JClVEzPusZpStzOJ6ROdavUQ1w3zHyR0z-r86f2fwLAAD__zcNikE) at work in December, alleging the automaker was aware of Ndiaga Diagne's "volatile temperament and propensity for aggression." Lillian Mendoza Brady, 65, claims Diagne attacked her as she tried to walk around him while he was praying at the facility. Tesla refused to disclose his identity or provide video of her encounter with him, but she [recognized him](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOkeDzU8oKLZJd7fdEo3xJLbugJFnuIS3X2VfYftPn845f77mL0ycttdvXGnS9zPPG53CpEplfqXC4lG-ST0yaz7KRldBP1uwvQFnYJwDJr7mtg6ThzA2NU3NMDjoWmuhjlMHXR_6tnX0hOCs9zSOTdcj3h0B3p91mj5n4GBsGnBuuIGzYbwPyz0ADX7pqhYoJM3lppGU3ihPvvIPlduS15qnqLpL5X5V9lHZx3metyUfRWM-hD4yn1llH0rCaGjdOV9EZmFMqxhJb41GtBCpkZizpu1l5JCdFjUoggcrBROpmDMmJpM3sxe8qBhfCL8r-6jLFPYzMSfph6qF14qJ_8Hp_yX9mezfAAAA__8QOo__) from reports about the deadly shooting. It seems like every piece of political news today is doom and gloom. Criticism. Everything is negative. Everything is about what is broken, what is corrupt, what is failing. America bad. Always.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QaHxD5x655OB3p_7V7TMWqmRaZFzz-EHcMTRUUPvTjE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190283811)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/50df85a7-44ea-4e00-ab8b-d724ac679793?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And to be honest, I'm part of that too. The Angry Democrat definitely leans into criticism. We talk about problems. We talk about what needs to be fixed. Everyone has opinions about what's wrong.
But the other day I was at a meet and greet with Bryan Hambley, and he started the event with a simple question that has been sticking with me for days.
A question we don't ask enough.
Not because we want to ignore the problems. Not because we don't see what needs fixing. But because, frankly, we have a pretty damn good country and pretty damn good lives in many ways.
The question was simple:
**What is something you are proud of?**
Something the United States has done.
Something your hometown has done.
It sounds easy. But it wasn't.
People struggled with it. Some would think of something they were proud of and then immediately follow it with why it's bad now, why it's being eroded, or why some politician is ruining it. We're so conditioned to talk about decline that we almost feel uncomfortable acknowledging success.
At the meet and greet people mentioned public education, national parks, NASA, and other things.
When I answered, I said the Great Lakes.
But the thing I'm actually most proud of about the United States is something else entirely.
And it took living abroad for me to fully understand it.
To see the full interview with [Bryan Hambley](https://substack.com/redirect/283f82da-f318-455f-82c8-2e58176856cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) please click the link below.
The Angry Ohioan
[Russo and Hambley: Two Democrats. One Office. Same Questions.](https://substack.com/redirect/bf76cc99-a3e7-4480-8df1-88651660492f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I recently sat down with former State House Minority Leader Allison Russo and Bryan Hambley. Both are Democrats running for Secretary of State here in Ohio...
[Listen now](https://substack.com/redirect/bf76cc99-a3e7-4480-8df1-88651660492f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
11 days ago * 7 likes * 1 comment * The Angry Democrat
* * *
## **Seeing America From the Outside**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QaHxD5x655OB3p_7V7TMWqmRaZFzz-EHcMTRUUPvTjE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190283811)
Some of you know that I lived in China from around 2005 until 2017. After that I spent about two years in Taiwan. I've also traveled to many other countries.
When you live abroad that long, you don't just visit. You navigate their systems.
You deal with landlords.
You sign contracts.
You open bank accounts.
You get a phone plan.
You start businesses.
You pay taxes.
You deal with bureaucracies and corruption.
You experience daily life inside another country's system.
And doing that changes how you see America.
It allows you to take experiences from other places and compare them to the United States. It allows you to crowdsource ideas and solutions from different systems.
But there is one thing I have never seen done better anywhere else in the world.
**The universality of American constitutional rights and the ability of people from anywhere to become part of Americanism.**
The United States is a beacon of inclusion.
Not perfect inclusion. But inclusion that is universal for all.
* * *
## **Equal Rights Under the Constitution**
Immigrants come to America from all over the world and become citizens.
And once they are here, they are protected under the same Constitution as everyone else.
They can open businesses.
They can buy property.
They can work.
They can criticize the government.
They can practice religion.
They can defend themselves.
They can vote once they become citizens.
It doesn't matter whether you speak with a New York accent or an Indian accent.
The rights are the same.
That is extraordinary.
You can walk into a strip mall in America and see a pho shop, a taco stand, a pizzeria, and a shawarma shop, all next to each other. Four different cultures. Four different accents. Four different origin stories.
All protected under the same law.
That level of everyday integration is something people who have never lived abroad often take for granted.
* * *
## **This Does Not Happen Everywhere**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QaHxD5x655OB3p_7V7TMWqmRaZFzz-EHcMTRUUPvTjE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190283811)
In many countries, being a foreigner means you will never truly belong.
You can live there for decades and still never be considered one of them.
You may not be able to own property.
You may not be able to open a business without a local partner.
You may need a spouse from that country just to register the business in their name.
Working in government? Forget it.
Even speaking the language with an accent can be enough to limit opportunity.
Meanwhile in the United States, naturalized citizens serve on school boards, run companies, sit in state legislatures, teach in universities, and operate businesses in every town in the country.
The only restriction is that you cannot be President unless you are born here.
Everything else is open.
That is uniquely American.
* * *
## **America 's Quiet Diversity**
We talk about immigration constantly in politics. But we rarely acknowledge what a massive success story American integration actually is.
Think about it.
I've been to about 40 states and countless small towns.
And I have yet to find a town without at least one of these:
A Mexican restaurant.
A Chinese restaurant.
A pizza shop.
Often all three.
For a country that is constantly accused of xenophobia, it's remarkable how even the smallest towns embrace some sort of cultural diversity in everyday life.
Yes, the Mexican restaurant might be Americanized.
Yes, the Chinese food might be Americanized.
But the people running those businesses are still immigrants.
And they are protected under the same laws as everyone else.
That phenomenon is far rarer globally than Americans realize. You don't see a immigrant American family in Wuzhou, China running a burger shop sending their kids to to school as the first generation, while running for office to join the Board of Education.
* * *
## **Why I Came Back**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QaHxD5x655OB3p_7V7TMWqmRaZFzz-EHcMTRUUPvTjE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190283811)
Living abroad taught me something important.
No matter how long I lived in China, I would never be Chinese.
No matter how long I lived in Taiwan, I would never be Taiwanese.
The same is true in many other countries.
But in America?
You can become American.
And once you do, the Constitution protects you the same as anyone else.
Freedom of speech.
Due process.
The right to own property.
The right to bear arms.
The right to criticize the government.
Those protections apply regardless of your accent, background, or where you were born.
I genuinely don't know if anything quite like that has existed before in world history.
* * *
## **Pride and Responsibility**
None of this means America is perfect.
But people who come here see that too.
They see the places where the country can grow and change. And because they come from different places, with different accents, different backgrounds, and different origin stories, they bring ideas with them.
All of those perspectives operating under the Constitution of the United States allows people to participate in government and civic life, to recognize what works well and what does not, and to contribute their own experiences to improving the system.
The universality of constitutional rights makes that possible. It allows everyone to take part.
It is also why so many people who came here, built a life here, and made something of themselves eventually feel a responsibility to give back.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3159258&post_id=190283811&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMjgzODExLCJpYXQiOjE3NzMwNTQ3OTEsImV4cCI6MTc3NTY0Njc5MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMxNTkyNTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.rcKz4T9u8ikmEGjqERKGj_9gi3zyJ_6puV54F5aoKMM)
## **Take a Moment**
So let me ask you the same question [Bryan Hambley ](https://substack.com/redirect/3e0ef422-0034-4bbe-b7fb-bc2bb3ec6ac1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)asked that night.
Stop reading for a second and think about it.
What is something you are proud of in the United States?
And don't allow yourself to start saying how it can be improved or how it is getting worse. Just acknowledge what you are proud of.
What are you proud of in your home state?
We've spent a lot of time criticizing America.
Sometimes rightfully so.
But pride in what works is not nationalism in a dangerous sense. It's recognition of the principles worth protecting.
America has survived nearly 250 years because of those principles.
And they're worth defending.

Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. Maybe it is time to remember what we love about America | | | Mar 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | It seems like every piece of political news today is doom and gloom. Criticism. Everything is negative. Everything is about what is broken, what is corrupt, what is failing. America bad. Always. | | ---|---|--- And to be honest, I'm part of that too. The Angry Democrat definitely leans into criticism. We talk about problems. We talk about what needs to be fixed. Everyone has opinions about what's wrong. But the other day I was at a meet and greet with Bryan Hambley, and he started the event with a simple question that has been sticking with me for days. A question we don't ask enough. Not because we want to ignore the problems. Not because we don't see what needs fixing. But because, frankly, we have a pretty damn good country and pretty damn good lives in many ways. The question was simple: What is something you are proud of? Something the United States has done. Something your hometown has done. It sounds easy. But it wasn't. People struggled with it. Some would think of something they were proud of and then immediately follow it with why it's bad now, why it's being eroded, or why some politician is ruining it. We're so conditioned to talk about decline that we almost feel uncomfortable acknowledging success. At the meet and greet people mentioned public education, national parks, NASA, and other things. When I answered, I said the Great Lakes. But the thing I'm actually most proud of about the United States is something else entirely. And it took living abroad for me to fully understand it. To see the full interview with please click the link below. The Angry Ohioan I recently sat down with former State House Minority Leader Allison Russo and Bryan Hambley. Both are Democrats running for Secretary of State here in Ohio... 11 days ago 7 likes 1 comment The Angry Democrat Seeing America From the Outside Some of you know that I lived in China from around 2005 until 2017. After that I spent about two years in Taiwan. I've also traveled to many other countries. When you live abroad that long, you don't just visit. You navigate their systems. You deal with landlords. You sign contracts. You open bank accounts. You get a phone plan. You start businesses. You pay taxes. You deal with bureaucracies and corruption. You experience daily life inside another country's system. And doing that changes how you see America. It allows you to take experiences from other places and compare them to the United States. It allows you to crowdsource ideas and solutions from different systems. But there is one thing I have never seen done better anywhere else in the world. The universality of American constitutional rights and the ability of people from anywhere to become part of Americanism. The United States is a beacon of inclusion. Not perfect inclusion. But inclusion that is universal for all. Equal Rights Under the Constitution Immigrants come to America from all over the world and become citizens. And once they are here, they are protected under the same Constitution as everyone else. They can open businesses. They can buy property. They can work. They can criticize the government. They can practice religion. They can defend themselves. They can vote once they become citizens. It doesn't matter whether you speak with a New York accent or an Indian accent. The rights are the same. That is extraordinary. You can walk into a strip mall in America and see a pho shop, a taco stand, a pizzeria, and a shawarma shop, all next to each other. Four different cultures. Four different accents. Four different origin stories. All protected under the same law. That level of everyday integration is something people who have never lived abroad often take for granted. This Does Not Happen Everywhere In many countries, being a foreigner means you will never truly belong. You can live there for decades and still never be considered one of them. You may not be able to own property. You may not be able to open a business without a local partner. You may need a spouse from that country just to register the business in their name. Working in government? Forget it. Even speaking the language with an accent can be enough to limit opportunity. Meanwhile in the United States, naturalized citizens serve on school boards, run companies, sit in state legislatures, teach in universities, and operate businesses in every town in the country. The only restriction is that you cannot be President unless you are born here. Everything else is open. That is uniquely American. America 's Quiet Diversity We talk about immigration constantly in politics. But we rarely acknowledge what a massive success story American integration actually is. Think about it. I've been to about 40 states and countless small towns. And I have yet to find a town without at least one of these: A Mexican restaurant. A Chinese restaurant. A pizza shop. Often all three. For a country that is constantly accused of xenophobia, it's remarkable how even the smallest towns embrace some sort of cultural diversity in everyday life. Yes, the Mexican restaurant might be Americanized. Yes, the Chinese food might be Americanized. But the people running those businesses are still immigrants. And they are protected under the same laws as everyone else. That phenomenon is far rarer globally than Americans realize. You don't see a immigrant American family in Wuzhou, China running a burger shop sending their kids to to school as the first generation, while running for office to join the Board of Education. Why I Came Back Living abroad taught me something important. No matter how long I lived in China, I would never be Chinese. No matter how long I lived in Taiwan, I would never be Taiwanese. The same is true in many other countries. But in America? You can become American. And once you do, the Constitution protects you the same as anyone else. Freedom of speech. Due process. The right to own property. The right to bear arms. The right to criticize the government. Those protections apply regardless of your accent, background, or where you were born. I genuinely don't know if anything quite like that has existed before in world history. Pride and Responsibility None of this means America is perfect. But people who come here see that too. They see the places where the country can grow and change. And because they come from different places, with different accents, different backgrounds, and different origin stories, they bring ideas with them. All of those perspectives operating under the Constitution of the United States allows people to participate in government and civic life, to recognize what works well and what does not, and to contribute their own experiences to improving the system. The universality of constitutional rights makes that possible. It allows everyone to take part. It is also why so many people who came here, built a life here, and made something of themselves eventually feel a responsibility to give back. Take a Moment So let me ask you the same question that night. Stop reading for a second and think about it. What is something you are proud of in the United States? And don't allow yourself to start saying how it can be improved or how it is getting worse. Just acknowledge what you are proud of. What are you proud of in your home state? We've spent a lot of time criticizing America. Sometimes rightfully so. But pride in what works is not nationalism in a dangerous sense. It's recognition of the principles worth protecting. America has survived nearly 250 years because of those principles. And they're worth defending. Stay Angry Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by support Matt's work. body:
Why I'm Running
| | | | |
---
| Russ Cleveland Candidate for U.S. House, MT-01
Small Business Owner • Dad • Coach • Navy Veteran
---
|
Hi Friend,
My name is Russ Cleveland. I grew up in the Bitterroot Valley in western Montana. I'm a small business owner who built a childcare company, a coach, a husband, a dad, and a Navy veteran. I'm running for Congress in U.S. House, MT-01.
This campaign didn't start in a back office in Washington, D.C., or because a party insider asked me to run.
It started in a hospital room with our daughter, Madison, who showed us what real courage looks like.
Almost six years ago, my wife Kate and I watched our thirteen-year-old take her last breath after an unexpected battle with leukemia.
While she was fighting for her life, we were also fighting insurance companies. Endless paperwork. Bills that reached $300,000 in a single month. A system that felt impossible to navigate.
When you sit in a hospital room like that, you learn something quickly.
The system isn't built for families like ours. We don't have lobbyists. We don't have PACs writing checks. All we have is one vote.
Too often that voice gets drowned out by dark money and special interests deciding which candidates are "viable."
I've chosen a different path.
One where we stop telling Montanans what they should want, and start listening to what they actually need.
And when you do that, something powerful happens.
You realize people aren't nearly as divided as those in power want us to believe. Most people just want someone who will show up, listen, and fight for them.
Madison never got the chance to grow up and chase her dreams.
I'm running because every child in Montana deserves the future Madison never got.
If you want to help us build something different, I'd be grateful for your support.

"If you have dozens of priorities, you have none. When I took office, I saw this laundry list of things that we said were priorities, none of which we were excelling at. That's why, when I became mayor, I said we would focus on only a few things: public safety, curbing homelessness, and making our streets as clean as possible. Today, San Jose is not just one of the safest cities in the state, but in the entire country."
I heard this from Matt Mahan a couple of years ago after he became mayor of San Jose in 2023. He was young, impressive, and purely solutions-oriented. But he also understood the human side of government. He had been a schoolteacher in the classroom and had young kids at home. "The goal of government should be to help people succeed and live the kind of lives they want." Pretty simple, straightforward mission statement.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a82990e6-90a4-4460-b940-e458b9e89da3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now, Matt is running for governor of California. "The spending of the government of California has gone up 60% in the past 5 years, to over $340 billion today. Has California gotten 60% better in that time? No one thinks it has." Indeed, California today is experiencing net population outflows primarily because it's gotten too expensive to live and raise a family. "I'm running for governor because I think I can make the government deliver more value for the people than we are currently getting."
One example Matt cited to me in my interview of him for the [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/480f82b6-5239-4e83-b2b8-f6caf3d0ee8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this week: "When I took office in San Jose, we had a homelessness program run by an organization that employed 40 outreach workers. They were averaging only 1 referral per month per worker. Now, it wasn't entirely their fault, as we also didn't have enough beds. But we shifted the resources to beds, and now we have only 10 outreach workers but they're much more productive because they actually have resources to offer a person on the street." Very common sense, but imagine that kind of recalibration across a budget of hundreds of billions of dollars. Matt worked in the private sector after his stint as a teacher so he understands how to effectively use resources. The potential benefit for the state and its people is enormous.
His campaign slogan is "[Back to Basics](https://substack.com/redirect/2ad6074a-3cd7-4695-a713-61edda863221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." A lot of our politics has devolved into arguing about this priority or that. Matt's approach is to get the machine of government actually delivering what it's supposed to. What a straightforward, yet critical, mission.
The governor's race in California is a non-partisan affair; the all-party primary is on June 2nd with the top two vote-getters proceeding to the general election in November. If Matt gets over 20% of the vote in June he will probably go to the general election, where I think he would be very tough to beat.
As you can tell, I'm enthused about Matt's campaign as I think it has enormous potential to improve the lives of tens of millions of Californians. For my interview of Matt, click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/8979f508-69c9-4171-8690-b986c12e63a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). To check out his campaign, including to donate (as I have), click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/2ad6074a-3cd7-4695-a713-61edda863221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I'm glad someone like Matt decided to make this kind of case in such an important race. He's got the track record to demonstrate what kind of governor he'd be. And if enough people see his message, I have no doubt that he'll be in Sacramento next year delivering massive wins for the people.
You know something we can all do better on? Our data. Go to [noblemobile.com/yang](https://substack.com/redirect/050d565b-3f6a-4a87-9eb2-58e623ae8a26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for 3 months off your wireless bill, the best deal around, that will also reduce your screen time and help you save for your family. subject: Deep Undercover: I changed everything, here's why . . .
body:
I went deep undercover — deeper than I've ever gone before. And I did it because the story demanded it. Because the truth was locked behind a door that only someone willing to completely disappear could open.
