| James O'Keefe | | | | | | [****](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) [****](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) Dear Patriot,

I need to tell you about what I just went through -- and why [**I need your help right now**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D).

For the past several weeks, **I 've been someone else entirely**.

Different voice. Different walk. Different bearing. Everything about the way I moved, spoke, and carried myself had to be unrecognizable. **My own team barely knew it was me**.

I went deep undercover -- deeper than I've ever gone before. And I did it because the story demanded it. Because the truth was locked behind a door that only someone willing to completely disappear could open.

I traveled state to state with my team. We lived out of hotels. We burned through operational expenses keeping our cover tight. Every detail had to be perfect -- because one slip doesn't just end the investigation. It can end careers. **It can put people in danger**.

This was one of the best performances of my career. And I mean that with full weight.
[ YES, I'LL SUPPORT JAMES AND OMG RIGHT NOW ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)
Before this investigation, we were still recovering from Minneapolis.

When the ICE riots broke out, I was already on the ground. While most journalists reported from a safe distance -- or from their living rooms -- **my team and I were in the streets**. Documenting. Recording. Putting ourselves between the chaos and the camera to make sure America could see what was really happening.

**The danger was real. The cost was real.**

Hotels. Equipment. Fuel. State-to-state travel. Operational security.

Disguises. The bills from this investigation have piled up -- and now they've come due.

[**I need to raise $52,000 in the next 10 days.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)

That's the real cost of what my team and I just did. And I won't sugarcoat it -- if we can't cover these expenses, it threatens our ability to fund the next investigation that's already in motion.

Here's exactly what your donation covers:

* [**$50**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- helps with one night of lodging for an undercover journalist in the field
* [**$100**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- keeps a team member operational on the road for a full day
* [**$250**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- helps fund a full day of undercover field operations
* [**$500**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- high-grade recording equipment that captures truth and protects sources
* [**$1,000**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- helps fund an entire week of an active investigation
* [**$5,000**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D) -- supports a full investigation from first contact to public release

[ YES, I'LL SUPPORT JAMES AND OMG RIGHT NOW ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)
I've spent my career proving that independent journalism -- real journalism, the kind powerful institutions genuinely fear -- is possible without corporate influence, without hedge funds, and without advertisers who tell you what stories to kill.

We've exposed the Secret Service. The FBI. Corporate cartels colluding to rig bids. **Government corruption at every level**.

**None of that happens for free. And none of it happens without you.
You are the reason OMG exists.**

I changed my voice, my walk, and my identity because I believe the American people deserve journalists who will go that far to get the truth. I put my team on the streets of Minneapolis because someone had to bear witness.

Now I'm asking you to be part of this.

[**Can I count on you for $50, $100, $250 -- or whatever you can give today?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)

We have 10 days. $52,000 to raise. **And another investigation already waiting**.
[ YES, I'LL SUPPORT JAMES AND OMG RIGHT NOW ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)
I'm deeply grateful for your support. It means more than I can say.

In Truth, James O'Keefe
Founder and CEO
O'Keefe Media Group

P.S. -- I went straight from this investigation into the next one because the story doesn't wait. But the bills are here now. Please help me cover what we spent and fund what's coming -- [**DONATE NOW**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D). Every dollar goes directly to field operations.

P.P.S. -- We're $52,000 short with 10 days on the clock. If 520 people give $100, we make it. If you know someone who believes in this work, please forward this email. [**DONATE HERE**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D).

The war on Iran has entered its second week, and is horrific in itself--but that's not the only war underway, and the whole is even more tragic than the sum of its parts.
Trump launched two undeclared wars on the same week in countries over 8,500 miles apart, neither of which have been authorized by Congress.
### **An inferno raging out of control**
The president initially promised that the war on Iran would be over in weeks, before reports [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/162e4c48-7f43-4133-a352-06c7307430d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Iran's military strategy appears to be depleting the Pentagon's limited supply of interceptor missiles, allowing the conflict to stretch on with no end in sight.
The interceptors on which Israel and the Gulf States have relied are vastly more [expensive](https://substack.com/redirect/57c83dd1-2e95-44b7-b938-167f812837b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than the Iranian drones and missiles they have countered, and take [years to replace](https://substack.com/redirect/bd4ef304-7fa3-4a93-9b21-f4e57583c740?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Meanwhile, Iran harbors an [arsenal](https://substack.com/redirect/ae5061aa-fc9f-4214-b083-89f72d56a09c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that [remains](https://substack.com/redirect/ea745fdd-7d07-4dae-aa6c-e718c466181a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the largest, most potent, and easiest to replace in the region, allowing an attrition strategy for which the Pentagon, and the global capitalist economy, are entirely unprepared.
It's almost as if Trump ducked into a punch from Iran directed squarely at Wall Street.
Beyond the human rights abuses en masse implicit in the Pentagon [bombing schools](https://substack.com/redirect/3f2d20b9-3b84-458a-8058-07456b3bf841?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and lighting the sky over Tehran [on fire](https://substack.com/redirect/56ab5992-bf35-49ff-86e2-2e3391c59fb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the inferno of the war on Iran has also extended to the U.S. through its profound--and still escalating--economic impacts.

In particular, China has [accelerated](https://substack.com/redirect/29e4c790-8be3-41ea-9bee-b668c328712c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its sales of U.S. treasury bills, sparking volatility in [bond markets](https://substack.com/redirect/d1308351-879c-42f2-9795-5329c7c522f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That volatility, in turn, threatens the role of the dollar as a global [reserve currency](https://substack.com/redirect/468acd43-970a-45c8-930a-7ff1d3f2ff4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and places pressure on interest rates, which the Federal Reserve is in a poor position to reduce due to inflation preceding last week's Israeli-American attacks on Iran.
The longer the Strait of Hormuz remains shut down, the higher oil prices will climb. That, like the president's tariffs, will inflate the price of more or less everything--at a time when working Americans are already [struggling](https://substack.com/redirect/7f7f54e7-6347-4261-993b-ad3c8f20bfbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to survive.
Finally, by striking at the oil infrastructure of the Gulf States aligned with Washington, Iran is threatening to [cut off](https://substack.com/redirect/8f66f35b-430a-424f-8c8b-ab08c1e06e96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a crucial source of capital that keeps Wall Street afloat. Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates all rely on security guarantees from Washington. But Washington has written figurative checks that the Pentagon appears unable to cash. As the Gulf States' production capacity grows increasingly limited, so will the [spigot](https://substack.com/redirect/be319760-cf13-419d-8fd3-4f4eb7af60d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that keeps the American economy afloat.
It's important to recognize that wars are not won or lost entirely on the battlefield. The economic impacts of the war on Iran are not only growing by the day, but appear to stand at the heart of Tehran's strategy. It's almost as if Trump ducked into a punch from Iran directed squarely at Wall Street.

But even on the battlefield, the war appears to be going a lot less well for the U.S. than officials would have us believe. From confirmed troop deaths, to official reports of damage to civilian infrastructure, to reports of Russian intelligence-sharing with Iran, the Pentagon has acknowledged casualties--and several risks that threaten more to come--while downplaying them in public.
That shouldn't surprise anyone.
From [Vietnam](https://substack.com/redirect/de3be232-6003-4f13-8eaf-b55ea606cdba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), to [El Salvador](https://substack.com/redirect/60ae0361-f3ea-479d-a9a3-38a654d0b258?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Nicaragua](https://substack.com/redirect/f5dfb8e6-c0cc-4706-b02c-bba823c5d74f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Iraq](https://substack.com/redirect/98e308e0-0441-4679-b273-0921b3a12ab1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Afghanistan](https://substack.com/redirect/2aeb85c9-6efd-4855-95bb-cd5f3e93571e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--conflicts spanning over 10,000 miles and 50 years--the Pentagon consistently downplayed casualties, costs, and future risks. One of the most important takeaways from those wars was that the U.S. intelligence establishment [can't be trusted](https://substack.com/redirect/4a44164d-9a82-4b44-92a1-e67f59840344?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Europe appeared to have [learned](https://substack.com/redirect/f78f9ad8-6a7b-494c-8db6-dba4888d002a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that lesson at one point, only to have [forgotten](https://substack.com/redirect/6c2b494a-0f80-48a3-b66f-22748ec1e7c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it immediately.
### **Washington wages war on the world**
Last week, the president launched military strikes not only [on Iran](https://substack.com/redirect/04f3e017-6ab0-407e-8e06-fb3c8a04ad2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but also in [Ecuador](https://substack.com/redirect/fb2d703d-5c28-4f1d-b24b-4edb56a64fab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
As dangerous as Trump's unrestrained violence has already become, congressional abdication in the face of his unconstitutional power grab might ultimately prove even more catastrophic.
Given the unfolding global economic catastrophe stemming from Iran's retaliation against the [new axis of evil](https://substack.com/redirect/6c2b494a-0f80-48a3-b66f-22748ec1e7c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it's easy to see why Ecuador might be widely overlooked. After all, the U.S. military deployment to Ecuador appears to be [supported](https://substack.com/redirect/fb2d703d-5c28-4f1d-b24b-4edb56a64fab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by that country's leadership, unlike in Iran.
But the mission appears [no more defined](https://substack.com/redirect/fb2d703d-5c28-4f1d-b24b-4edb56a64fab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than in Iran, even though Ecuador's conservative President Daniel Noboa Azín claimed that it would include fighting "narcoterrorism and illegal mining."
What we do know is that Trump launched two undeclared wars on the same week in countries over [8,500 miles apart](https://substack.com/redirect/04f3e017-6ab0-407e-8e06-fb3c8a04ad2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), neither of which have been authorized by Congress.

The Constitution [explicitly grants](https://substack.com/redirect/ff43ac60-e023-49cf-99f2-75ce75f693dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Congress the power to declare war--and with good reason.
The Founders feared presidents sparking wars to contrive domestic support. They might not have specifically envisioned a president launching wars to evade accountability for sex trafficking crimes documented in the Epstein files, but they foresaw the pattern and tried to stop it.
Withholding the power to declare war from the Executive branch was the subject of [specific](https://substack.com/redirect/96ed93a1-ad6a-4fc1-8f7f-b37cd2d42221?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) discussion during the Constitutional Convention. Putting Senators [Lindsey Graham](https://substack.com/redirect/5391ae38-e89a-44ed-8682-4ed08febafa0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (R-SC) and Tim Scott (R-SC) to shame, two of South Carolina's delegates to the convention (Charles Pinckney and John Rutledge) argued in 1787 to limit the power of the Executive Branch. Pinckney [suggested](https://substack.com/redirect/aebadab7-a95f-4186-b37d-a1cbfbfd8f5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that allowing warmaking powers "would render the Executive a Monarch, of the worst kind...an elect[ed] one."
Beyond Iran and Ecuador, it remains important to recall last year's [attack](https://substack.com/redirect/57f89b87-dcf3-4f75-b690-d6a8e809d400?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Venezuela--another war never authorized by Congress.
As dangerous as Trump's unrestrained violence has already become, congressional abdication in the face of his unconstitutional power grab might ultimately prove even more catastrophic.
In this context, it grows increasingly dire that voters replace the congressional [authoritarians](https://substack.com/redirect/1ac3a1d0-fb9a-4118-9813-235e4e71b711?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in both corporate political parties, ideally with [new voices](https://substack.com/redirect/eee10d70-d2fe-400b-9d62-d32ff9858bbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who understand the Constitution, the limits it places on executive power, and the crucial responsibility of Congress to enforce them.

### **A circular firing squad**
Republicans and Democrats [alike](https://substack.com/redirect/3ef204ea-65aa-4b0c-bba9-0462d195ba1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Congress have played a key role in empowering Trump. They [funded](https://substack.com/redirect/1771584a-b625-4748-b79c-d5822f321b8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his budgets, failed to restrain him when [they](https://substack.com/redirect/f9fd80e6-ea2c-4826-b679-c8484b61f77d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had a [chance](https://substack.com/redirect/79b22fdc-a55f-4b26-97a4-e4b21dbf8778?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (both last week and during his [first](https://substack.com/redirect/cc37e99b-e27c-409c-ac96-d00886b13f1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) term), and continue to [pledge](https://substack.com/redirect/6111dccc-667f-4160-9585-4ad6d23c91ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) fealty to Israel even as Netanyahu uses the Pentagon like his personal plaything.
That's why it's remarkable to witness cracks in the dam. They might have been encouraging, had they come sooner.
Tillis faulted Noem not for the authoritarian policy agenda they ultimately share, but because her overzealousness was exposing its brutality and turning the public against it.
Last week, I [described](https://substack.com/redirect/d2df695f-00bd-4ee3-b549-f39d7d79cd5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the long overdue firing of DHS secretary Kristi Noem as "blood in the water." It seems that she is not the only cabinet figure whose days may be numbered.
It was not public awareness or ridicule that brought Noem down. She has, after all. been the object of [plenty](https://substack.com/redirect/3b6afe1f-61bd-4e0e-9e3c-0851d6ebca20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of legitimate popular criticism since she took office. What finally forced her expulsion from the cabinet was the defection of Republican senators, including one with nothing to lose.
Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) is retiring next year, at the conclusion of his current term. While policymakers who hope to continue their careers seem uniformly intimidated by the president and the cult of personality that enables him, Tillis acted like an actual Senator last Monday, [rebuking](https://substack.com/redirect/21750abd-ca57-4289-87f3-556cd3bb1016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Noem in forceful terms that drew applause from observers:
> [W]hat we've seen is a disaster under your leadership, Ms. Noem, a disaster. What we've seen is innocent people getting detained that, turns out, are American citizens.
Trump fired her days later. He was well-advised to do so, since GOP defections in the Senate can effectively force the president's hand. Put simply, the president can't afford to lose the votes of Republican Senators, even with key Democrats serving as [lapdogs](https://substack.com/redirect/6111dccc-667f-4160-9585-4ad6d23c91ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Israel.
Just to be clear, Tillis is no constitutional hero. He went on [suggest](https://substack.com/redirect/21750abd-ca57-4289-87f3-556cd3bb1016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that:
> We're beginning to get the American people to think that deporting people is wrong. It's the exact opposite....
>
> Law enforcement, we've got to have their back. We've got to make it clear when they make a mistake, then they get corrected for it, but you don't walk away from it, and you've done it too many times now....
In other words, Tillis faulted Noem not for the authoritarian policy agenda they ultimately share, but because her overzealousness was exposing its brutality and turning the public against it.

Yet, despite being a right-wing conservative, Tillis was willing to force the president to fire the DHS Secretary who he had previously praised. And he might not be done yet.
Last week, I speculated that Secretary of War / former FOX News host Pete Hegseth would be the next to follow Noem out of Washington. After all, he has proven just as clownish and [incompetent](https://substack.com/redirect/0325cdd3-7c6d-4d45-901c-7fecd27cbc15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as Noem, and he's publicly [admitted](https://substack.com/redirect/f53e9b87-b7a9-424a-8fd5-af6527cda4ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Trump has expressed dissatisfaction with his performance (although a viral photo depicting Trump [yelling](https://substack.com/redirect/b36be851-b9a2-4060-8087-ef55d146563a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at him through a White House glass door appears to be fake).
Sen. Tillis, however, appears to have more immediate concerns about another fascist demagogue in Washington: White House advisor Stephen Miller. Asked on CNN whether he thought Miller "should go," Tillis [replied](https://substack.com/redirect/30a2d04a-aabe-4d11-9734-3f1b9fd162d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Oh, of course I do.....He's a big problem in this administration. He has been from the beginning.
Unlike Noem, Miller does not lead an executive department requiring congressional appropriations to operate. In other words, Tillis had leverage over the president with respect to Noem that he lacks with respect to Miller.
But antagonized GOP Senators can still complicate the president's plans--unless, of course, he manages to entice Democrats to cast votes aligned with their GOP colleagues. Having voted against the proposed Senate war powers resolution, Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) is the most obvious example, but Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) has also [affirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/6111dccc-667f-4160-9585-4ad6d23c91ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his primary allegiance to Israel, which might lead him to [continue](https://substack.com/redirect/1771584a-b625-4748-b79c-d5822f321b8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) empowering Trump.
While Miller being forced out of the White House would be a tremendous victory for the grassroots movements around the country [challenging](https://substack.com/redirect/91bcd1df-131e-4b80-9cec-59bc0d2764a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) mounting abuses by ICE and other DHS agencies, it would come far [too late](https://substack.com/redirect/fc8bdea6-71b0-4a9f-a241-5065e99a721d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for any number of people, including Renee Good and Alex Pretti.

"The kids are allright"
say adults impressed
by their insight, intelligence
even their wisdom
as if their necks
were unburdened by yokes
placed in some cases
by the very same voices

They see the knives
in the hands of their parents
and their bosses and
banks and wrinkled men in suits
protruding from
their bleeding backs.
The kids may be smarter
than all the adults
but their days
are all numbered

the adults--know it

# **Statement from Del. Sam Rasoul:
Senate Kills HB1075, Rejects Lowering ApCo Costs**
---
_Delegate Sam Rasoul introduced HB1075 to lower costs for Appalachian Power rate-payers, but the Senate declined to pass this bipartisan effort to save Virginians money_ _._
---
**Roanoke, VA -** Virginia State Delegate Sam Rasoul issued the following statement on the Virginia Senate's rejection of HB1075: **" Electric bills are too high, and the Senate failed to act," **stated Delegate Rasoul.** "Each bill we kill that brings everyday Virginians relief is a failure to serve those who elected us. This bill would have targeted high fuel costs, and passed the House with bipartisan support."** **"Many people are paying over $1000/month on energy that cost less than half that not even a decade ago. It is unacceptable that we continue to allow ApCo rate increases. This is a clear case of profits over people."** Appalachian Power has increased rates 159% since 2007, more than three times the rate of inflation. **When Raja told me he wanted to run for Senate, it was a no-brainer, I knew he was the right person for the job****. **

At the very end of February, the United States entered into--well, let's just call a spade a spade--a war with Iran alongside Israel. The Trump Administration launched an operation they called "Epic Fury," which many rightfully pointed out sounded like it was named by someone who had spent a little too much time on _Fortnite_.
And as we heard from Fox substitute anchor turned Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Trump hater turned Trump fangirl Secretary Marco Rubio, the United States had successfully pulled off this war/not a war/end to a 47-year-long war/military operation without a hitch--despite having U.S. military members killed and one of our jets being shot down by friendly fire from Kuwait.
But as this was going on, there was another trend popping up time and time again from the White House down the chain of command, all the way to the online MAGA influencers.
[It started on March 3 ](https://substack.com/redirect/e136c8cf-00e1-4ad4-9623-7110cb47fb17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)when a story broke that a unit commander told non-commissioned officers
that the Iran war was part of God's plan to usher in the End Times and bring about Jesus Christ's second coming, according to a complaint filed with a religious freedom watchdog.
The Military Religious Freedom Foundation (MRFF) has fielded more than 110 similar complaints about commanders in every branch of the U.S. military between the war's start on Saturday morning and March 2, [reported journalist Jonathan Larson on his Substack page](https://substack.com/redirect/ad005a43-fb8f-4775-abe1-72f344f7e0e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the group told him the complaints came from more than 40 different units stationed in at least 30 military installations.
The complaint stated:
> "He said that 'President Trump has been anointed by Jesus to light the signal fire in Iran to cause Armageddon and mark his return to Earth.' He had a big grin on his face when he said all of this, which made his message seem even more crazy."
These are hardly the only instances of this.
Secretary Pete Hegseth has become the de facto preacher of the 2nd Trump Cabinet, [starting off events at the White House with prayers to "King Jesus."](https://substack.com/redirect/625e0d0f-6976-4a78-b2a6-d15982c1d426?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[He also stated at a press conference](https://substack.com/redirect/24f4a628-4bbd-44c6-b224-af2efe1b9ddf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) following the launch of Operation Epic Fury-where he also danced around not committing to keeping boots off the ground-that "when I pray every day for [our troops] and for this mission-I pray simply for the biblical wisdom to see what is right and the courage to do it."
And even our elected leaders on Capitol Hill joined in on this rhetoric, with S[peaker Mike Johnson](https://substack.com/redirect/e1a13c97-27d6-43da-bb8f-d51ecbbb4f18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[who has long held apocalyptic views and committed acts in that same vein, like helping to transport five red heifers from Texas to Tel Aviv](https://substack.com/redirect/a74fbc1e-5027-4049-8985-1b69213febc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--saying that Iranians have "a misguided religion."
[Senator Lindsey Graham](https://substack.com/redirect/ccc22646-8553-4732-a4db-fbebd96ad265?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) didn't even try to bury the lede, saying out and out to the press that "this is a religious war and we will determine the course of the Middle East for a thousand years."
And then you had your religious leaders and influencers from around the MAGA universe chiming in and capitalizing on the moment.
Texan televangelist and chairman of Christians United for Israel--the largest Zionist organization in America--[Pastor John Hagee led his congregation](https://substack.com/redirect/3b602e50-e8af-48cb-a956-c1f756eed517?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in thanking God "for the fabulous military victory over the enemies of Israel " and "for our president, Donald Trump, whose wise courage has crushed the enemies of Zion."
Lance Wallnau, another prominent Texas televangelist associated with the New Apostolic Reformation (NAR) and the Seven Mountain Mandate, [celebrated the attack](https://substack.com/redirect/4cf475cf-6168-4e94-9142-bcdc2cbf0096?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Iran, declaring Trump to be "a prophetic instrument of God" who "has an assignment to protect Israel" and now "the return of Jesus is back on the menu."
So if you haven't been following this as closely as some of us have, you probably have one reaction right now, which is:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/88f266f0-8720-44c8-bdde-ca647274fe98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Yes, it's hard not to feel like, despite everything these people are saying about religious fanaticism in the Middle East--and to quote Marco Rubio again, who said "Iran is run by lunatics, religious fanatic lunatics"--that we are in fact the ones in _The Bad Place_ with the religious zealots running our country.
But you might be asking yourself a few questions, and with good reason:
Why is a religion based on peace so hell-bent on war and destruction?
Why are Christians so invested in the State of Israel and its defense?
And why are we all of a sudden centering Christianity in our military operations?
Well, if you will join me, let's go once again down the rabbit hole of Evangelical Christian Nationalism and what it's doing to our politics.
## **Fire and Brimstone**
Modern-era Christianity, across most sects, has largely been seen as a peaceful religion. Jesus Christ is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world and is the provider of peace and goodwill to all who inhabit the Earth.
However, American Evangelicals often view Jesus much differently than that.
Similar to their choice between charity and the Prosperity Gospel, they do not view Jesus primarily as the peaceful lamb. They see Jesus as the Lion--the one who roared into the Temple, flipping over tables and ejecting the money changers.
As Kristin Kobes Du Mez details in her book _Jesus and John Wayne_ , Evangelicals like Jerry Falwell "couldn't stomach 'effeminate' depictions of Christ as a delicate man with 'long hair and flowing robes.' Jesus 'was a man with muscles. . . . Christ was a he-man!'"
It's why, during Iran-Contra, Falwell promised Reagan he would help get his message out "in layman's language," and he did so by taking out full-page ads in major newspapers deriding "freezeniks," "ultralibs," and "unilateral disarmers" who were undermining Reagan's efforts to rebuild the nation's military strength.
"We cannot afford to be number two in defense!" he warned.
Dr. Edwin Louis Cole, the father of the so-called Christian Men's Movement, had no use for "sissified" portraits of Jesus that failed to reveal his true character.
"Christlikeness and manhood are synonymous," he insisted, and to be Christlike--to be a man--required "a certain ruthlessness."
These evangelicals want Christ as King and Warrior because they genuinely believe that Armageddon will be a physical battle in the Holy Land, and they want every ounce of force and strength imaginable to ensure victory over the forces of evil.
Those militant depictions of faith, mixed with apocalyptic theology, also led to movements preparing for this Great Battle.
The Quiverfull movement, which takes its name from Psalm 127:4-5, encourages members to have as many children as possible, because "culture wars and holy wars need as many soldiers as possible."
Virginian evangelist Samuel Davies once said in 1758, speaking to Christians before the French and Indian War, that "even the God of peace proclaims by his providence to arms, and the art of war becomes part of our religion."
Now you have modern Christian Nationalists like William Wolfe during the Biden Administration echoing Davies and saying "we are getting close" to a point where Christians will have to "heed the call to arms."
"To be ruled by cowards in a time of war is a curse, because God hates cowards," [Wolfe added at a ](https://substack.com/redirect/7ec16afe-0831-4769-b27b-d84bfc9efaab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Jesus and Politics](https://substack.com/redirect/7ec16afe-0831-4769-b27b-d84bfc9efaab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ conference.](https://substack.com/redirect/7ec16afe-0831-4769-b27b-d84bfc9efaab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
These depictions of Christ as warrior, militant faith, and the End Times-as-war mindset inextricably link Evangelicals' male-dominated culture war to the real physical wars being waged by conservative administrations in the Middle East.
Just like those families building their ranks through large numbers of children, they believe the U.S. military should be as strong and as large as possible.
They do not believe that the meek shall inherit the Earth.
They believe the strong will take it by force at the end of the world.
The United States must maintain a large and powerful military to join Christ at the Mount of Olives at Armageddon.
And where is this battle supposed to take place?
Where is the Mount of Olives located?
In the modern-day Levant--where Israel is located.
And who was prophesied to be the enemy in this battle?
The nation of Elam, east of Babylon, was historically associated with the Persian Empire--modern-day Iran.
## **The Evangelical Obsession with Israel and the Middle East**
Most people understand how important Israel is to the Jewish faith, as it is a Jewish state.
What many people are surprised to learn is that Israel's existence is arguably even more important to American Evangelicals.
After all, the largest zionist organization in the US is [Christians United for Israel.](https://substack.com/redirect/c8e447e2-17f2-4a7e-9e7d-16d5e3da2499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A large part of American Evangelical Christianity is built upon apocalypticism and Zionism in order to fulfill that apocalyptic theology.
The Christian Far Right has a fanatical obsession with ensuring that the United States maintains a close alliance with Israel and guaranteeing Israel's continued existence--because securing an ally in that region will mean direct access to the site of Armageddon once the end times begin.
And some already believe they have begun.
Why do these Christians consider themselves Zionists?
One word: **dispensationalism.**
[Dispensationalism](https://substack.com/redirect/5231b146-70cd-4c87-a62e-3a675622638d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) iis an evangelical theological system that interprets the Bible through a literal historical lens, dividing human history into distinct "dispensations," or eras of God's administration. It emphasizes a strict distinction between Israel and the Church, premillennialism, and a pre-tribulation rapture.
Within this framework, modern Israel is viewed through a prophetic lens.
The re-establishment of Jewish sovereignty in the Levant is seen as a necessary step toward the end times.
It is sometimes described as "Armageddon Theology"--a vision of the future where Jews and non-Christians are destroyed while believers ascend to heaven.
It's why so many of these far-right Christians are comfortable sending billions of dollars in military aid to Israel.
It's why Donald Trump invested so much political capital in Israel, sending his son-in-law Jared Kushner as his emissary and even moving the U.S. embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem during his first term.
It's why many far-right Christians openly call for wiping Palestine off the map--figuratively or literally--because they believe all of that land must ultimately fall under the control of a Western ally.
It's why former Arkansas governor and Baptist minister Mike Huckabee is now the ambassador to Israel.
Many people scratched their heads at that decision.
But it makes complete sense when viewed through the lens of dispensationalism.
Their goal is not to support a Jewish state.
It's not even truly to support Israel.
It's an **ends-justify-the-means arrangement.**
## **Jesus Is Coming, Look Busy**
You may have noticed a number of Evangelical influencers posting TikToks of themselves dancing with captions like:
"We're at war with Iran! Me: Knowing Jesus is coming back."
[Former OnlyFans star turned conservative influencer Nala Ray](https://substack.com/redirect/5041810c-6af8-48c8-9ac6-5e4185cfc345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) posted one such video.
And maybe your reaction was simply: _well that was weird._
Even putting aside the "let them eat cake" attitude toward the loss of human life in war.
But again, with dispensationalism, Evangelicals' literal interpretation of the Bible leads them to believe the end of days and the return of Jesus Christ will come through a literal war in that region against a Middle Eastern power.
They believed it during Iran-Contra.
During Operation Desert Storm.
During Operation Iraqi Freedom.
During the Global War on Terror.
And now during Operation Epic Fury.
Some believe this so deeply that they think they can **speed up the end times** by creating conflict in the region.
They do this in several ways:
[Many American Christians are actively trying to fund the rebuilding of the Third Temple](https://substack.com/redirect/ed6fbd42-c5ea-4860-94c1-5fba392415bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Jerusalem on the Temple Mount--an effort tied to eschatological expectations primarily within Orthodox Judaism.
[Speaker Mike Johnson helped facilitate the delivery of red heifers to Israel](https://substack.com/redirect/5d50e0f8-8ef3-4ee9-83ed-d7da6f509de9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) while the country was carrying out a genocide in Gaza, because it is believed that a red heifer must be sacrificed during a war to initiate the end of days.
But the primary way they influence events is through political power.
Through positions inside presidential administrations.
Through alliances with lobbying groups and super PACs like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), which support congressional candidates willing to sign blank checks for military aid to Israel and back U.S. intervention in the region.
Because war in the Middle East means Jesus might be returning soon.
And the more conflict there is, the more they believe prophecy is unfolding.
It becomes a kind of theological **" hurry up and wait."**
Which is exactly why having a deeply ideological Christian at the head of the U.S. military--like Pete Hegseth--is such a liability.
We don't know how far some of these actors are willing to go to bring this worldview to fruition.
And the more they use Christian-coded language and Bible verses on Department of Defense social media accounts--and the more the Secretary of Defense publicly leads prayer services tied to military action--the more it appears that they see the U.S. military as a vehicle to fulfill their theological prophecy.
It does not appear they are ending forever wars in the Middle East anytime soon.
And when those people also have influence over the man holding the nuclear codes, the consequences could be catastrophic.
## **Know Your Enemy**
The more we understand how these people operate, the better we can work against their goals--no matter how fanatical those goals may be.
These self-described Christian Nationalists are not operating on the fringes of American politics anymore. They are continuing to make their way into the halls of Congress, state legislatures, federal agencies, and even the White House. [Evangelical preachers now regularly pray over President Trump in the Oval Office](https://substack.com/redirect/2e9b115a-78c2-4218-9c3c-3efc954829a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and their theological worldview increasingly bleeds into the language and policy priorities of the administration itself.
**And the most important thing to understand about these movements is that they are not operating randomly**.
They have a framework. They have institutions. They have funding.
And they have a worldview that tells them they are not simply participating in politics--they are participating in a cosmic struggle between good and evil.
These far-right Christian Nationalists are constantly searching for signs of the End Times, and they will frequently shoehorn almost any major cultural or political development into that framework.
When Social Security numbers were first proposed, [evangelical preachers condemned them as "the mark of the beast."](https://substack.com/redirect/97605a4e-9192-49ef-ba3e-354d92e9a953?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Many did the same thing with barcodes in grocery stores during the 1970s and 80s.
More recently, some claimed COVID-19 vaccine cards were the mark of the beast.
Others insisted the vaccine itself was the mark.
The "mark," of course, comes from the Book of Revelation, where it is described as a sign of the impending apocalypse and the rise of the Antichrist.
Their literal interpretation of scripture leads them to believe that the Book of Revelation is not metaphor or allegory, but rather **history written in advance**.
And if Revelation is history told ahead of time, then every war, every technological development, every political shift must be interpreted through that lens.
Every generation of believers tends to assume they are living in the final chapter of human history. But within modern American Evangelicalism, that belief has been weaponized and turned into a political organizing tool.
Because if you genuinely believe that you are living in the final days before Armageddon, then normal political restraints stop mattering.
Compromise becomes weakness. Pluralism becomes betrayal. Democracy itself becomes optional.
After all, if you believe you are fighting the literal forces of evil before the end of the world, why would you feel obligated to follow the same rules as everyone else?
That is how a religious movement becomes a political one. And eventually, how it becomes a governing ideology.
The perversion of religious doctrine to fit political ambition has created a feedback loop that pulls more and more people into this worldview. Evangelical Christianity places enormous emphasis on conversion--bringing as many people as possible into the fold during one's lifetime.
But for many believers shaped by apocalyptic theology, that mission carries an even deeper urgency.
A large portion of Evangelical Christians believe that at the end of the world there will be a literal battle between the armies of good and evil. Jesus will lead the army of Good, composed of every person who accepted Him during their lifetimes. Satan will lead the army of Evil, made up of everyone else.
That belief does not simply shape personal faith. It shapes how adherents view politics, diplomacy, war, and international alliances.
Every election becomes a battlefield. Every foreign policy decision becomes a step toward prophecy. Every conflict in the Middle East becomes a potential sign that the clock is running out.
And if that is how you interpret the world, then escalating conflict is not necessarily something to avoid. It might actually be something to encourage. Which is exactly why this ideology becomes so dangerous when it begins to influence the highest levels of government.
Because if the people making decisions about war, nuclear weapons, and global diplomacy genuinely believe they are helping to bring about the end of the world as part of God's plan, then the consequences of those decisions become impossible to predict.
At that point, policy is no longer being guided by strategy, diplomacy, or even basic self-preservation.
It is being guided by prophecy.
And prophecy, unlike policy, does not require evidence.
It only requires belief.
## **The End (of Times) Justifies the Means**
The danger of Christian Nationalism is not simply that it blurs the line between church and state.
It is that it replaces politics with theology.
When people who hold these beliefs gain power, war stops being a tragedy to avoid and starts becoming a sign that history is unfolding the way it is supposed to.
Conflict becomes validation. Escalation becomes faith. And peace becomes an inconvenience that delays the inevitable.
That is why the rhetoric surrounding Iran, Israel, and the Middle East coming out of the current administration should alarm anyone who believes in the basic principles of secular government.
Because when political leaders begin talking about foreign policy in the language of prophecy, they are no longer just governing a country.
They are trying to fulfill a story. And the problem with trying to fulfill an apocalyptic story is that it has only one ending.
The Book of Revelation does not end with diplomacy.
It ends with war.
Which means the more influence these movements gain over American politics, the more the rest of us may find ourselves dragged into a conflict that was never about national security, democracy, or even geopolitics.
It was about proving that the end of the world had finally arrived.
And that is not a foreign policy.
That is a death wish masquerading as faith.
## **TL;DR**
Many American Evangelicals and Christian Nationalists do not just view the Middle East through the lens of geopolitics -- they view it through the lens of prophecy.
Rooted in a theology called **dispensationalism** , they believe that wars involving Israel and Iran are signs that the biblical End Times are approaching and that Jesus Christ will soon return.
This belief helps explain why many on the Christian Right aggressively support Israeli expansion, escalating conflict in the region, and even frame modern wars as part of **God 's plan**.
When those beliefs begin influencing U.S. foreign policy and military leadership, the risk is no longer just bad strategy -- it's the possibility that global conflict is being justified as a step toward **Armageddon.**

The nation of Elam, east of Babylon, was historically associated with the Persian Empire--modern-day Iran. The Evangelical Obsession with Israel and the Middle East Most people understand how important Israel is to the Jewish faith, as it is a Jewish state. What many people are surprised to learn is that Israel's existence is arguably even more important to American Evangelicals. After all, the largest zionist organization in the US is A large part of American Evangelical Christianity is built upon apocalypticism and Zionism in order to fulfill that apocalyptic theology. The Christian Far Right has a fanatical obsession with ensuring that the United States maintains a close alliance with Israel and guaranteeing Israel's continued existence--because securing an ally in that region will mean direct access to the site of Armageddon once the end times begin. And some already believe they have begun. Why do these Christians consider themselves Zionists? One word: dispensationalism. iis an evangelical theological system that interprets the Bible through a literal historical lens, dividing human history into distinct "dispensations," or eras of God's administration. It emphasizes a strict distinction between Israel and the Church, premillennialism, and a pre-tribulation rapture. Within this framework, modern Israel is viewed through a prophetic lens. The re-establishment of Jewish sovereignty in the Levant is seen as a necessary step toward the end times. It is sometimes described as "Armageddon Theology"--a vision of the future where Jews and non-Christians are destroyed while believers ascend to heaven. It's why so many of these far-right Christians are comfortable sending billions of dollars in military aid to Israel. It's why Donald Trump invested so much political capital in Israel, sending his son-in-law Jared Kushner as his emissary and even moving the U.S. embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem during his first term. It's why many far-right Christians openly call for wiping Palestine off the map--figuratively or literally--because they believe all of that land must ultimately fall under the control of a Western ally. It's why former Arkansas governor and Baptist minister Mike Huckabee is now the ambassador to Israel. Many people scratched their heads at that decision. But it makes complete sense when viewed through the lens of dispensationalism. Their goal is not to support a Jewish state. It's not even truly to support Israel. It's an ends-justify-the-means arrangement. Jesus Is Coming, Look Busy You may have noticed a number of Evangelical influencers posting TikToks of themselves dancing with captions like: "We're at war with Iran! Me: Knowing Jesus is coming back." posted one such video. And maybe your reaction was simply: well that was weird. Even putting aside the "let them eat cake" attitude toward the loss of human life in war. But again, with dispensationalism, Evangelicals' literal interpretation of the Bible leads them to believe the end of days and the return of Jesus Christ will come through a literal war in that region against a Middle Eastern power. They believed it during Iran-Contra. During Operation Desert Storm. During Operation Iraqi Freedom. During the Global War on Terror. And now during Operation Epic Fury. Some believe this so deeply that they think they can speed up the end times by creating conflict in the region. They do this in several ways: in Jerusalem on the Temple Mount--an effort tied to eschatological expectations primarily within Orthodox Judaism. while the country was carrying out a genocide in Gaza, because it is believed that a red heifer must be sacrificed during a war to initiate the end of days. But the primary way they influence events is through political power. Through positions inside presidential administrations. Through alliances with lobbying groups and super PACs like the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), which support congressional candidates willing to sign blank checks for military aid to Israel and back U.S. intervention in the region. Because war in the Middle East means Jesus might be returning soon. And the more conflict there is, the more they believe prophecy is unfolding. It becomes a kind of theological " hurry up and wait." Which is exactly why having a deeply ideological Christian at the head of the U.S. military--like Pete Hegseth--is such a liability. We don't know how far some of these actors are willing to go to bring this worldview to fruition. And the more they use Christian-coded language and Bible verses on Department of Defense social media accounts--and the more the Secretary of Defense publicly leads prayer services tied to military action--the more it appears that they see the U.S. military as a vehicle to fulfill their theological prophecy. It does not appear they are ending forever wars in the Middle East anytime soon. And when those people also have influence over the man holding the nuclear codes, the consequences could be catastrophic. Know Your Enemy The more we understand how these people operate, the better we can work against their goals--no matter how fanatical those goals may be. These self-described Christian Nationalists are not operating on the fringes of American politics anymore. They are continuing to make their way into the halls of Congress, state legislatures, federal agencies, and even the White House. , and their theological worldview increasingly bleeds into the language and policy priorities of the administration itself. And the most important thing to understand about these movements is that they are not operating randomly. They have a framework. They have institutions. They have funding. And they have a worldview that tells them they are not simply participating in politics--they are participating in a cosmic struggle between good and evil. These far-right Christian Nationalists are constantly searching for signs of the End Times, and they will frequently shoehorn almost any major cultural or political development into that framework. When Social Security numbers were first proposed, Many did the same thing with barcodes in grocery stores during the 1970s and 80s. More recently, some claimed COVID-19 vaccine cards were the mark of the beast. Others insisted the vaccine itself was the mark. The "mark," of course, comes from the Book of Revelation, where it is described as a sign of the impending apocalypse and the rise of the Antichrist. Their literal interpretation of scripture leads them to believe that the Book of Revelation is not metaphor or allegory, but rather history written in advance. And if Revelation is history told ahead of time, then every war, every technological development, every political shift must be interpreted through that lens. Every generation of believers tends to assume they are living in the final chapter of human history. But within modern American Evangelicalism, that belief has been weaponized and turned into a political organizing tool. Because if you genuinely believe that you are living in the final days before Armageddon, then normal political restraints stop mattering. Compromise becomes weakness. Pluralism becomes betrayal. Democracy itself becomes optional. After all, if you believe you are fighting the literal forces of evil before the end of the world, why would you feel obligated to follow the same rules as everyone else? That is how a religious movement becomes a political one. And eventually, how it becomes a governing ideology. The perversion of religious doctrine to fit political ambition has created a feedback loop that pulls more and more people into this worldview. Evangelical Christianity places enormous emphasis on conversion--bringing as many people as possible into the fold during one's lifetime. But for many believers shaped by apocalyptic theology, that mission carries an even deeper urgency. A large portion of Evangelical Christians believe that at the end of the world there will be a literal battle between the armies of good and evil. Jesus will lead the army of Good, composed of every person who accepted Him during their lifetimes. Satan will lead the army of Evil, made up of everyone else. That belief does not simply shape personal faith. It shapes how adherents view politics, diplomacy, war, and international alliances. Every election becomes a battlefield. Every foreign policy decision becomes a step toward prophecy. Every conflict in the Middle East becomes a potential sign that the clock is running out. And if that is how you interpret the world, then escalating conflict is not necessarily something to avoid. It might actually be something to encourage. Which is exactly why this ideology becomes so dangerous when it begins to influence the highest levels of government. Because if the people making decisions about war, nuclear weapons, and global diplomacy genuinely believe they are helping to bring about the end of the world as part of God's plan, then the consequences of those decisions become impossible to predict. At that point, policy is no longer being guided by strategy, diplomacy, or even basic self-preservation. It is being guided by prophecy. And prophecy, unlike policy, does not require evidence. It only requires belief. The End (of Times) Justifies the Means The danger of Christian Nationalism is not simply that it blurs the line between church and state. It is that it replaces politics with theology. When people who hold these beliefs gain power, war stops being a tragedy to avoid and starts becoming a sign that history is unfolding the way it is supposed to. Conflict becomes validation. Escalation becomes faith. And peace becomes an inconvenience that delays the inevitable. That is why the rhetoric surrounding Iran, Israel, and the Middle East coming out of the current administration should alarm anyone who believes in the basic principles of secular government. Because when political leaders begin talking about foreign policy in the language of prophecy, they are no longer just governing a country. They are trying to fulfill a story. And the problem with trying to fulfill an apocalyptic story is that it has only one ending. The Book of Revelation does not end with diplomacy. It ends with war. Which means the more influence these movements gain over American politics, the more the rest of us may find ourselves dragged into a conflict that was never about national security, democracy, or even geopolitics. It was about proving that the end of the world had finally arrived. And that is not a foreign policy. That is a death wish masquerading as faith. TL;DR Many American Evangelicals and Christian Nationalists do not just view the Middle East through the lens of geopolitics -- they view it through the lens of prophecy. Rooted in a theology called dispensationalism , they believe that wars involving Israel and Iran are signs that the biblical End Times are approaching and that Jesus Christ will soon return. This belief helps explain why many on the Christian Right aggressively support Israeli expansion, escalating conflict in the region, and even frame modern wars as part of God 's plan. When those beliefs begin influencing U.S. foreign policy and military leadership, the risk is no longer just bad strategy -- it's the possibility that global conflict is being justified as a step toward Armageddon. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. # [Unpacking 10 Days of Iranian Conflict](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4399133&post_id=190389531&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMzg5NTMxLCJpYXQiOjE3NzMwNjQ1ODAsImV4cCI6MTc3NTY1NjU4MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQzOTkxMzMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.QZp4agtiB6CcPiC4GsCd0Zc-GEEaoPGgSIKwIFTIlRg)
### No one in Washington can answer what the endgame is.
| | [Patrick J. Murphy](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa)
---
| Mar 9

We are now ten days into the U.S. and Israeli war against Iran. Here's where things currently stand.
Israeli and American strikes have severely degraded Iran's nuclear program. Much of Iran's naval capacity has been destroyed; by President Trump's count, [42 ships](https://substack.com/redirect/77b346f5-1864-488f-95d6-43c8cdae755e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) now sit at the bottom of the ocean. For the [first time since World War II](https://substack.com/redirect/8f517dac-5b6d-4c95-850a-3bfa7d18c02b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a torpedo was used to sink an enemy vessel. The Pentagon has also leaned on artificial intelligence to identify targets, deploying technology developed through its recent partnership with [OpenAI](https://substack.com/redirect/43f4221e-e219-41e4-8648-49a082ae8bb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
## **New Developments**
The war has killed [seven American troops](https://substack.com/redirect/db8e8576-a322-4809-b524-93bc79b45a3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), at least 1,230 people in Iran, at least 397 in Lebanon, and 11 in Israel.
The leadership ranks of the regime have also been hollowed out at a stunning pace. Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and more than forty of Iran's most senior military and intelligence officials have been killed.
Unfortunately, as President Trump said himself, "The attack was so successful it knocked out most of the candidates" to lead Iran. "They're all dead. Second or third place is dead." The _[New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/76c27d3b-7f71-4cdf-9815-0bd9ae005f8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ also reports that an Israeli strike also killed another group of Iranian officials the White House had identified as more willing to negotiate.
Yesterday, Iran named Ayatollah [Mojtaba Khamenei](https://substack.com/redirect/a8fffb0d-8bf9-4095-853c-137f980fbd10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as the Supreme Leader's successor. He is one of the sons of the country's late supreme leader, and is considered more hard-line and volatile than his father. His wife was also killed in the same strike that killed his 86-year-old father last weekend.
It remains unclear what the political endgame of this war is. No doubt we set back Iran's nuclear ambitions back in June with Operation Midnight Hammer, and again these last ten days. What does it mean to win when nobody in Washington has bothered to define what's next?
If you find my writing on these topics helpful, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..fYoeDhAgaU5-oS-_kOE04icjGSno7N_TVH_xEK46xZA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=190389531)
## **What is the Goal?**
Trump's stated military objectives are straightforward enough: destroy Iran's nuclear capabilities, eliminate its ballistic missiles, and demolish its navy. But his political objectives are a different story.
It's unclear if he's aimed at regime change or something else. He has recently indicated that he is indifferent to Iran's future after the military campaign ends. But on Friday, he said he would be directly involved in choosing Iran's future leader and committed to Iran's long-term future. At the same time, he also said he's okay with leaving the clerical regime in place as long as they treat the U.S. and Israel "fairly." Still, he calls for "unconditional surrender."
Most experts agree it's nearly impossible to achieve regime change purely from air strikes, so the theocratic clerical rule is likely to endure with the current strategy. This assessment is backed by the [National Intelligence Council](https://substack.com/redirect/29eae233-fa2a-4a72-b794-132dd2cb6dc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The [former head of Israeli military intelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/7f14e770-e5a6-40c1-88ac-5c249119f1a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Amos Yadlin, told CBS that even if 99% of Iran's military capacity is destroyed, it only buys three to four years of peace.
Currently, the [U.S. is weighing the option of sending special forces](https://substack.com/redirect/28f42a0a-6c35-4416-ae4a-ced177bea799?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to seize Iran's nuclear stockpile. The regime has 450 kilograms of 60%-enriched uranium, which can be converted to weapons-grade within weeks. According to Axios, if the entire stockpile reached 90% purity, it would be enough material for 11 nuclear bombs.

Securing Iran's enriched uranium would be one of the hardest tasks left in this operation. Much of the material is believed to be stored deep underground, and officials acknowledge that no one is entirely certain where all of it is right now. Most of the stockpile sits in the underground tunnels of the nuclear facility in Isfahan, while the rest is split between Fordow and Natanz. It would also require nuclear scientists to aid combat soldiers on this mission.
# **Kurdish Resistance**
There is another alternative to the U.S. sending its troops that has been floated: arming the Kurdish resistance movement.
According to [CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/bdfff0b5-0df0-411b-98fd-38a94700a639?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the CIA has spent months courting Iranian and Iraqi Kurdish opposition groups, discussing a potential ground offensive to foment a popular uprising inside Iran. The U.S. discussed arming them and providing air support.
But the Kurds aren't just looking for a military role. They want political power. One Kurdish opposition group, the PJAK, a U.S.-designated terrorist group, in talks with the CIA, has told Washington it wants a say in who leads post-war Iran. And underneath that ask is the older, deeper one that's animated Kurdish politics for a century: self-determination. An independent Kurdish state, or at minimum meaningful autonomy, carved out of a collapsed Iran. The 30 million Kurds- 9 million of whom live in Iran- are among the [largest stateless ethnic groups in the world](https://substack.com/redirect/685505af-35e1-4fb5-8ebe-e31fd71e121e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Trump has already reversed course on this, though, telling reporters aboard Air Force One that he'd [ruled out Kurdish involvement](https://substack.com/redirect/6e5bc5ba-1959-453f-83c4-fcca48c0499b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "The war's complicated enough," he said.
One Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) official said, "We are staying neutral as Iraqi Kurds because there is no clarity for us on what the U.S. policy is. Is it full regime change? Or just a change in personnel?"
# The War Hits Home
The first week of war has already cost [$6 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/76c27d3b-7f71-4cdf-9815-0bd9ae005f8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That doesn't include a $1.1 billion U.S. radar system Iran reportedly destroyed in Qatar, or the full cost of missile interceptors. [Each Patriot missile runs around $4 million](https://substack.com/redirect/d7aa5159-26c8-4951-901a-1118e83f3694?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and reports suggest we've been firing as many as 11 to intercept a single incoming Iranian missile. The Pentagon is preparing an emergency funding request of up to $50 billion -- a mechanism critics are already comparing to the post-9/11 "Overseas Contingency Operations" fund that ultimately ballooned past $2 trillion for Iraq and Afghanistan.
Then there's the surging gas prices.
Roughly 20% of the world's oil moves through the Strait of Hormuz. On a normal day, about 80 tankers pass through. Last Tuesday, according to the _New York Times_ , approximately one did. Shipping companies have parked their vessels out of safety concerns and insurance premiums for vessels in the conflict zone have gone through the roof. As of this morning, [crude oil soared to $120](https://substack.com/redirect/c35f4eec-0301-412f-8749-7c0eda4df2c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a barrel, the highest level since 2022. The downstream effects on gas prices, shipping costs, and global markets are already here. The average price of gas by the gallon [rose nearly 27 cents](https://substack.com/redirect/4bee452c-83d7-4552-9b92-77ece288b06d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week. When I got gas this morning, it was $4.50 per gallon for 91 octane.
## **Could Cuba Be Next?**
When it comes to authoritarian countries, Trump says invading Cuba would be "[icing on the cake.](https://substack.com/redirect/8137bb73-da23-4ce4-8e60-cad02c395d7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"

At the newly launched "[Shield of the Americas](https://substack.com/redirect/c524335e-7831-42cd-a0f2-8c763892c367?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" summit in Doral, Florida, on Saturday, President Trump gathered leaders from more than a dozen Western Hemisphere nations, including Argentina, Chile, Costa Rica, Ecuador, and Panama, to formally launch a regional security coalition targeting cartels, migration, and foreign influence. But the main focus of the whole gathering was the future of Cuba.
Trump told the assembled leaders that several had privately urged him to intervene. "Four of you said, actually, 'Could you do us a favor? Take care of Cuba.'"

The timing is notable as Cuba is currently facing a [severe fuel shortage](https://substack.com/redirect/a4eb18a1-0098-42d9-9d33-5a799ec08241?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that has triggered nationwide blackouts, including outages that recently left the western half of the island without power.
The president has repeatedly pointed to the recent U.S.-backed transition in Venezuela following the capture of Nicolas Maduro as a model for how regime change could unfold elsewhere in the hemisphere.
Trump has tasked Marco Rubio to lead negotiations with Raul Castro's grandson, who controls the Cuban military, the real power base on the island. The framework reportedly on the table includes secure exile for regime figures, economic reforms, and a Cuban commitment to distance itself from Russia and China.
Some Cuba analysts say Havana could actually deliver on most of those asks without much difficulty. Release political prisoners, cooperate on migration and counternarcotics, guarantee no security agreements with Beijing or Moscow.
