Hi there, **As a national leader in the fight to preserve voting rights, VRF endorses and funds champions of democratic values and electoral access.** That’s why we’re coming to you to share some history about the enduring impact of the _Voting Rights Act_ (VRA), with a focus on its role in advancing racial enfranchisement in the United States. From dismantling language barriers to ensuring fair district maps, the VRA has been instrumental in expanding access to the ballot. At VRF, we support voting rights champions who share our values and are committed to defending the right to vote for every eligible American. Last year marked the 60th anniversary of the Voting Rights Act. We celebrate this milestone by recognizing the VRA’s transformative role in American democracy and renewing our commitment to protecting the rights it enshrined.

* * *
**The Origins of the Voting Rights Act** Before the passage of the VRA in 1965, two key constitutional amendments laid the groundwork for racial enfranchisement. The 14th Amendment guaranteed equal protection under the law, while the 15th Amendment prohibited racial discrimination in voting. Yet despite these legal protections, Southern states employed widespread voter suppression tactics, including poll taxes, literacy tests, intimidation, and violence to disenfranchise Black voters. Civil rights leaders and organizations like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., the NAACP, the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, and the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee mobilized a national movement to demand meaningful voting rights protections. The mass mobilization and public pressure from widespread non-violent demonstration and lobbying members of Congress culminated in the passage of the Voting Rights Act. The VRA prohibited discriminatory voting practices and provided federal oversight for jurisdictions with a history of racial discrimination. The VRA’s core provisions include:
* Section 2, which bans any voting law or practice that discriminates on the basis of race or color.
* Section 4(b) and Section 5, which together established “preclearance” requirements for certain jurisdictions to obtain federal approval before making changes to voting laws. Although the Supreme Court significantly weakened this provision in Shelby County v. Holder (2013), states like Maryland have since reinstated their own preclearance laws to preserve protections.

* * *
**Breaking the Language Barrier** The fight for inclusive access did not stop in 1965. In 1975, Congress amended the VRA to include Section 203, requiring jurisdictions with significant language-minority populations to provide bilingual voting materials and support. This reform was critical to enfranchising communities where English is not the dominant language. Today, some jurisdictions are using innovative tools to further expand access. In 2024, polling places in Denver trialed [handheld translation devices](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/pRqQrclJgcJoGwEdkfnYCkoDrdoTvQ2NDWv5h43moTgbqenqPFO3TmGtP9rRyFHF9lp_BdKfuZEHG75etKwesgCfPpMjeid04MhzbBZcR9efOlTnBMSIIn77BWm3wLBXjRmkMLb2FQeEEJo7SMsFUIZVmW94JlnUM9p4D4p7nBMikdH8j4VLPTnIy4osIe-oBWM41ayRwLblOXOeyLReKxCOGVrM9lQUU_p8sLQbKV5F5aqWuP3ntE1xb3FOouTqkY1ySBbBsLVBr1pWUIFIFRSE1Xi-7mi9nJ13ZFufeYNf369VStQDmnhiSfTQHBWVYDMcc0rFuSB9ncS_jHhvYexnOeo9-2YrwXVAHG8V7WWzDBxi-ZwQ7BJ6C6Vi_OkUXfernJuQYJdchoICyabKppggJWbox3ky1b2QQ5LaYeIpUe3nNgkxMBWIzo-qyB5e2pqy4yVriikW7iyR_jIkzPs0N4RmgBnuqnq_oifPlg1Aa6wBaqXmMrmbJ6eoOrtNe1hFNnHiddCXFt_hBDGvJblryiEsVlY3B2LH6zSqehOLDD5aWucixm2SYLlPIXdR5tzt_7-Jd9DHi_xexseWQD58Zni-r4vzbY5x-l5vJMfUleYTPt-jzYcXmENildDtxsGJJmhjwbngBiFnHU59CEIm5pul4cB-oMhuGHkh69qqXwoc5aON6ZmXaE4iyRQu4t8x9EMonzV7HwR27lGB0HySI_2zm_ceU78-mPvcwWFaOUH_iUwtIhiIIgUNpR5lz8ZUziQI6fluRVRayaff3meEUJ8P4-aQWSwBEVzuGFsRgcHo702W8y76Zp3irwNUtfwGmy52iqy8RUUvr7RIwBHkrq72O9XajYnLyuLosI5ifjkUWQZakOlOiE4Mp11LbRqGo3iH0_cQQXRT__LV_NZ71-IfEdug7r5Da_kCphIzYgZiDnKoWtFSwdV3zLjRFlMxhJB9GKJsbcWFxQdcq1pARm6d0WCsWpP386OEfcGugqjwSpt0Wqp709UcyI61bsulMkjoMpzK4c1c_WZ5IqLW0u9FCv3GC_s8qNRE_9H7Y3BJf81kiSBaM8LiIWfgYFGVRPzDIbeIzbniJlW8uI1rF7_8MusN6QnCSNp8pnUlGZp9NzYPXSMs4DNuFbrCsBSABaHMwajU-wslPYgBc9WllGAcXzm675wbXBAnjNo3U2GgzRxoZAuPSDWKGB7AnCZUXM1PQ68-nP7b3IFR7Xlh9HG8lrb1ufPIrLtJPZ_bwlQMHHSi8nQBKmr48UKxFBXNDHYbUvDmsz1_pE6AM0A6hKCYFIeoxjSpWE5S7U2EO1jzVG6TxcuoFA/DVlXUQaf82BlqUnn8TeMj-OdpHffyXyV/18), offering real-time language support in over 80 languages.

* * *
**The Census and Redistricting: The Fight Against Gerrymandering** Every 10 years, the U.S. Census provides vital demographic data used to redraw electoral district boundaries. This redistricting process is essential to maintaining equal representation, but it has been used to manipulate district borders to suppress voter power. Gerrymandering tactics like packing (concentrating voters of one group into a single district) and cracking (spreading them across many districts to dilute their influence) remain major threats to fair representation. Although the VRA sought to combat these practices, the Supreme Court’s 2019 decision in _Rucho v. Common Cause_ ruled that federal courts cannot adjudicate cases of partisan gerrymandering, leaving enforcement to the states. Since then, some states have acted to restrict gerrymandering, while others have moved in the opposite direction. In Texas, lawmakers have redrawn district maps ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, ahead of the normal decennial cycle, raising alarms about the potential for manipulation. The newly proposed map would potentially increase the amount of [Republican controlled districts to 79%, up from 66%](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/ClyPMvtqQLsuYtai9P6fFovX3jfv4yjrHWrYXeYlhsEPYH5n9frZFVlRo2n11L6cxnJ2MuiSaweDeuiUvODt-TqAcQBEbQ8MxW-0N4xki_JaXi4FGdIoBjtZ6fwr_QfHO6RDaV5VxA6ZKulCfcexgONQXn3hOMSO7TuzwpjStuq9LZ_K89E7Fc5IhkuF380gUgkeTDyXpnd70BQzdYbl4a_JPJiXRiZWO3VeZix5a25p0u4EdgsNvtXYUgObmy07rdSWks9d5bOUo-hVFUhPEx21a8ieiw7DKljqTAPPgNF-HYB9EsCjRHjZX1YDkPoZq6wYsfnWLr8rPjbmzzAL2WvSlkllNuQM3qBgzR-g9i0WBy30O7e3pURLjA70Xx8JYvprmxjHxISEbBt4SER3VAEVePxmKqqaZb2w6U6PnKynHtfi1jfvuPcfW10JQvJocn0LcDWQNTXoIRSrjJebZhQwxdcoKRFZkw/TML0UbDXXdLII8IBAEJlPi1CNUhylNrd/18). Other states, like New York and California, are also reviewing their processes. California, notably, uses an independent redistricting commission and bans partisan gerrymandering in its constitution. [](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/e1KU5sIZdyOopIHSYH6R4ZRK8gatI75-Kh_unUrx5o8NRcj5T9jWbJUcww3IX_tHQ1iuvTs5is5t4YHAs1oSKib-EgsCSR0GZ843rPcLRJLBOe5ikOpl17Zq6GcDP_nN61zGCfyaQGaJufM1_QXc_Zjatz4Lc5PyrjG13uv18YqadCZv6lTiEx-oqBazLCD09TUcSdxpIWd5Fo6S_L_lYS4b0LQxsXMMYJojbed5ifoCRr4qZwHgw5WN9YGkNqgR9t-S0A97KDN4I_M10Lm8zAHQ049ezSSLnGSci601OkaUmHdFyY78wS1By0EJiZjRBHIxE6VBTgjQaLiBZu02cvWVH8vhuCc1eC2brbiYCpsCUs9xrT7aL4WbWgs3Hzr4qSi8cQ-XuEJDdlf991hhrVp9nrJvymF8xGJWTpRBRuQvMwujx1x3LBOMi-pL_G2BXb7CNQ67T0jHGQDF532ewhM3FO-WQEGLWzfwACuM1qPchI7CJzfjQ3vSKmd69P9igXJfbMLxBF0_y1ahKz59OisikTu5KKif4yxSVnBVPxU91_PDh5ZhXJ5Et-OL3SjuuU2MPgRBp3FERIW-4QN2KoIt05x1fOqvI9uIV1tlVVzfq05Ux5jK9OHlwaHoL9Q9bERs5nUZnM5MpIiGesq3JYTj2UfSjlDbHbjIMLMpxiTDUoNKcT-WL60i5UYm7nSrwj5MIT8H0QLDESno6QYCfvaMgpZSoBvnIIQwAIK9ie4ZYo6FQmA5S1qBiCQJj50Ln1VVqViUsWWQ0ZwS-2ErdR1HHh_Xf2rsmL9_en4Ow20mJdh-74UtvRWIc99KYAh8S77NztBKyBD9Y59GtMq19Ge6tPkXzyawNJybfeAPyYHLL42BXCoyJ0coM4DzXu-WiSGy9Se1bhLsLH7KfqiKAZJAMei8oMEYwCAWdNRoLBC0/Q84WXv6V39VvtZoBJYBpXCOpJTfnuw7e/18) Undercounts in Census data, particularly among low-income voters and communities of color, further complicate redistricting. The consistent underrepresentation of these groups has, historically, skewed representation and disenfranchised these communities. That’s why VRF supports redistricting reforms that protect against bias and uphold the principle of “one person, one vote.” VRF also supports the highest quality data collection and equitable systems for apportioning votes.

* * *
**Conclusion: Celebrating 60 Years of Progress and the Work Ahead** The fight for racial enfranchisement has spanned generations. The Voting Rights Act remains a cornerstone of American democracy, responsible for expanding access, securing representation, and ensuring fair elections. As we look back at the law's impact, VRF honors the work of those who made it possible and we recommit ourselves to the cause. Today, VRF-endorsed leaders are working to strengthen these protections by advancing the _John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act_ , which would restore and improve key provisions of the original VRA. This legislation aims to increase access to the ballot, protect against discrimination, and promote equity in representation. To support our work or learn more, visit our [website](http://links.votingrightsfund.org/s/c/76bN0YaJ1MBB_5yCUEWwLXhXKsIJD8wty-zv4ZgD8gdGMmRyoR9rmFloHJp8CQ420XX4r-VolbcuKeFPl9tOOFrPHWLETtFDfgR7swb9FCNdNDtAoWVvXUMAcrHd8q8pejSvFtE4DZM9-M2s9cNMPXNj6cvl0vkoN7Iu3AWthX2J2-QrnBg8owLywbmXJ47ge0d89u0UW1pJHlLer0fFkTop43VuvwFPaiL0GZiDAEudNjThZX9RLYel8QIDtBI6rgHU1YrmhiWECWi8nJDlgv5TCIoBkMey3hvVYAcgQMd3OjCIUPnZKi7Vn18EHgMQ71tEyiViRO148rMCrtUZl64lEUP75O2oDDChpUY7WL2PgHGhhA376p3yrsU7f2Q/F_fOSUBQJeIuME3w3GG8qNFFxOxtPlcn/18) or consider making a contribution today. — Voting Rights Fund

clean_body: | | | Hi there, As a national leader in the fight to preserve voting rights, VRF endorses and funds champions of democratic values and electoral access. That’s why we’re coming to you to share some history about the enduring impact of the Voting Rights Act (VRA), with a focus on its role in advancing racial enfranchisement in the United States. From dismantling language barriers to ensuring fair district maps, the VRA has been instrumental in expanding access to the ballot. At VRF, we support voting rights champions who share our values and are committed to defending the right to vote for every eligible American. Last year marked the 60th anniversary of the Voting Rights Act. We celebrate this milestone by recognizing the VRA’s transformative role in American democracy and renewing our commitment to protecting the rights it enshrined. The Origins of the Voting Rights Act Before the passage of the VRA in 1965, two key constitutional amendments laid the groundwork for racial enfranchisement. The 14th Amendment guaranteed equal protection under the law, while the 15th Amendment prohibited racial discrimination in voting. Yet despite these legal protections, Southern states employed widespread voter suppression tactics, including poll taxes, literacy tests, intimidation, and violence to disenfranchise Black voters. Civil rights leaders and organizations like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., the NAACP, the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, and the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee mobilized a national movement to demand meaningful voting rights protections. The mass mobilization and public pressure from widespread non-violent demonstration and lobbying members of Congress culminated in the passage of the Voting Rights Act. The VRA prohibited discriminatory voting practices and provided federal oversight for jurisdictions with a history of racial discrimination. The VRA’s core provisions include: Section 2, which bans any voting law or practice that discriminates on the basis of race or color. Section 4(b) and Section 5, which together established “preclearance” requirements for certain jurisdictions to obtain federal approval before making changes to voting laws. Although the Supreme Court significantly weakened this provision in Shelby County v. Holder (2013), states like Maryland have since reinstated their own preclearance laws to preserve protections. Breaking the Language Barrier The fight for inclusive access did not stop in 1965. In 1975, Congress amended the VRA to include Section 203, requiring jurisdictions with significant language-minority populations to provide bilingual voting materials and support. This reform was critical to enfranchising communities where English is not the dominant language. Today, some jurisdictions are using innovative tools to further expand access. In 2024, polling places in Denver trialed , offering real-time language support in over 80 languages. The Census and Redistricting: The Fight Against Gerrymandering Every 10 years, the U.S. Census provides vital demographic data used to redraw electoral district boundaries. This redistricting process is essential to maintaining equal representation, but it has been used to manipulate district borders to suppress voter power. Gerrymandering tactics like packing (concentrating voters of one group into a single district) and cracking (spreading them across many districts to dilute their influence) remain major threats to fair representation. Although the VRA sought to combat these practices, the Supreme Court’s 2019 decision in Rucho v. Common Cause ruled that federal courts cannot adjudicate cases of partisan gerrymandering, leaving enforcement to the states. Since then, some states have acted to restrict gerrymandering, while others have moved in the opposite direction. In Texas, lawmakers have redrawn district maps ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, ahead of the normal decennial cycle, raising alarms about the potential for manipulation. The newly proposed map would potentially increase the amount of . Other states, like New York and California, are also reviewing their processes. California, notably, uses an independent redistricting commission and bans partisan gerrymandering in its constitution. Undercounts in Census data, particularly among low-income voters and communities of color, further complicate redistricting. The consistent underrepresentation of these groups has, historically, skewed representation and disenfranchised these communities. That’s why VRF supports redistricting reforms that protect against bias and uphold the principle of “one person, one vote.” VRF also supports the highest quality data collection and equitable systems for apportioning votes. Conclusion: Celebrating 60 Years of Progress and the Work Ahead The fight for racial enfranchisement has spanned generations. The Voting Rights Act remains a cornerstone of American democracy, responsible for expanding access, securing representation, and ensuring fair elections. As we look back at the law's impact, VRF honors the work of those who made it possible and we recommit ourselves to the cause. Today, VRF-endorsed leaders are working to strengthen these protections by advancing the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act , which would restore and improve key provisions of the original VRA. This legislation aims to increase access to the ballot, protect against discrimination, and promote equity in representation. Democrats' Shutdown Chaos Hits Airports

The Democrat-driven DHS shutdown is now ruining spring break for millions of Americans. TSA lines stretched [up to three hours](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyc0LvOnTAQBOCngc7ItwOHwkUauj9tSrSxl8NKviCvgeTtI_IIfzfNjD7Nr6_1CyhS_vyEhM5ftIYS1lbPdBDzicxwIfh2xkYJ2qqlHoU0Qs5rjqvqg_NhNLpHp6bJyNmqUfW726x6B70p_5onbaVV1pjtd8D3y4RxVrIn9yxJI2et5azVYIKCl53AyDdYgKmz8jwCNOTBl8xYL2h0IeVcnlTy4Evqo9tbO7gzPzq9dHq573vYyp-M91NLnV6OEqmR504vYWexQ0pYWQRMLMqFVQDVo9QmGP1Zqf0VkTKygERBbGcOlD8iwsHYVxeOm2IkHh_eJwHF_4r2jeMup_8FAAD__x7UgHg) at major airports, including Houston's Hobby Airport, New Orleans, and Atlanta, over the weekend. DHS blasted Democrats for holding travel "hostage for political points," with a spokeswoman calling it a [direct result of their](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL2OoCAUhZ8GOwx_g2NBsY3dbLulucIdJUEwXMR9_I37CNOd4uScL9-fr_ULYop5_w0nOt_jGkpYW73PKxLdSAQdwbc7tXhCW5VQlgvNxbzmtMohOB-sVgM6OU1azEZaORwOlZeopd2sCN_e-m_ctmA-5k2gFFbCEN27JLSYlRKzkqMOEj7MBFp8ggGYmBH3FaAhjb5kwtqhxY4x5_KmkkdfziG5o7WLmP7F1MLU8jzP-AAdMe-tZPwLZ8xY3ypTS6vQMTG1GPNpZmOYWiDWq9TG_QGFOJKH9F7yqyLRXZFXpJI68nAQ30vHmk_MjdNxt1CezNQyVBeuJ6YUyb7U-wkx_YdrP_DZnfoXAAD__w0ViT0) refusal to fund the department. TSA agents face their first full missed paycheck on March 14 -- the same day peak spring break travel kicks off -- and airports are telling travelers to arrive four to five hours before their flights. ★★★

President Trump told Fox News he is ["not happy"](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckL0OnDAQhJ8GOiP_cHAULtJcd2lTosW7HE78g-wF7vEj8gjpRiN9o0_z6z2_wQefPj8hknWnnzHjzOWIu6_1oFrhJHB8BPYReNZSD0IaIac5hVm1aB0ORrdk1TgaOfVqUO1mnVkeT_MYcVIrLLSSItQjGrc8zWrGqfX2XpJGTlrLSavOoIJHP4KRT-gBxqaXx47AVDuXU6VyAvuTfEr5Tjl1Lsc22I15r4350ehXo1_XdXVr_ia6bizeTS4BG_06qqiQ3E0Siph_Mywg_mwQKZEXCSKh8AVSFYm-LOqxF4okAgFSEbAyFbECb1SqQALeRKE9F65tsbhfPgRfh1v7E8GHf3b8H4eeVv8NAAD__yOEir8) with the selection and had previously called the younger Khamenei "unacceptable." Trump Draws Line: No Bills Until SAVE Act Passes

Sending Americans to war is the most serious decision a president can make – it’s not an “option” for a president to dangle. The American people deserve the truth, not cryptic threats from a White House that lacks the courage to serve our country themselves or to be honest about why this war of choice was started. = | = Thanks for being in this fight. — Seth | | | ---|---|--- About Seth Moulton Seth Moulton is a Marine and a Democrat with a mission to bring a new generation of leaders to Congress. # MEDIA RELEASE
# KEVIN KIJEWSKI REACTS TO AG DANA NESSEL'S DECISION NOT TO APPEAL DISMISSAL OF POLITICALLY MOTIVATED CHARGES AGAINST ALTERNATE ELECTORS – CALLS FOR END TO LAWFARE IN MICHIGAN
---
[|
---](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=6a6b73d070&e=4b10910eed)
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
**BIRMINGHAM, MI** – Kevin Kijewski, Republican candidate for Michigan Attorney General and attorney for Clifford Frost, today applauded Attorney General Dana Nessel's decision not to appeal the district court's dismissal of all charges against Frost in her failed alternate elector prosecution. This announcement marks the final defeat in Nessel's two-year political witch hunt, confirming the court's finding of insufficient probable cause and vindicating Frost completely. ****
"Today's decision is a **total vindication and a damning indictment of Dana Nessel's abuse of power** ," said Kijewski. "For years, Nessel weaponized her office against Republicans, as she herself admitted in 2023 when she called the alternate electors 'brainwashed' and boasted about shopping the case to a 'very Democratic-leaning county' to secure biased jurors.**She even acknowledged they lacked criminal intent and couldn't plead guilty because they believed they acted lawfully**. If that's not lawfare, I don't know what is. Nessel's refusal to appeal now admits what we knew all along: this was politics, not justice. **It's telling that her press release blames the 'district court's failure' to bind over the charges** when, in reality, **it was Nessel's own failure to build a legitimate case** — passing the buck after years of partisan pursuits."
Kijewski, who **successfully defended Frost and secured the dismissal** in September 2025, emphasized that Nessel's prosecution was a blatant attempt to criminalize political participation and silence dissent. "**This case was never about the law — it was about sending a message to conservatives**. As Michigan's next Attorney General, I'll end this kind of partisan lawfare once and for all, restore trust in our elections, protect constitutional rights, and focus on real threats to our communities, not vendettas against political opponents."
The charges stemmed from the 2020 alternate electors who, amid election disputes and following historical precedents like the 1960 Hawaii contest, submitted contingent certificates. Kijewski's highlighted the lack of criminal intent, leading to the court's decisive ruling. **"Freedom isn't negotiable, and neither is justice,"** Kijewski added. "This final nail in the coffin of Nessel's case shows why Michigan needs a fighter ready to stand up to government overreach from day one."
A copy of Kijewski’s brief in the case that sought the dismissal can be viewed by visiting [https://tinyurl.com/kdkdismissalbrief](https://kevinformi.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=39782b0ca6b504d2faad7a196&id=c157e3772a&e=4b10910eed).

As Michigan's next Attorney General, I’ll fight to uphold the rule of law, prosecute dangerous criminals, protect our Second Amendment rights, stop political prosecutions, and defend the hardworking people of this state from government overreach.
Very truly yours,Kevin KijewskiCandidate for Michigan AG

Washington State has long been a leader in election security and engagement. Yet, instead of looking for ways to improve what’s already working, some are proposing new burdensome requirements that make it harder for people to vote, without adding security.

It’s nothing more than political gamesmanship, and it helps no one – especially when we’re talking about something as fundamental as the integrity of our elections.

[I’ll keep fighting to defend voting rights for Washingtonians and Americans everywhere, Peter, but I need to know you’re with me. You’re probably wondering what I’m doing in your inbox. The truth is: I’m nervous about the upcoming elections, and how our democracy is at stake.
That’s why I’m reaching out to you on behalf of my friend, Roy Cooper.
Roy has spent his entire career as a public servant fighting for everyday North Carolinians. He helped expand health care access, revitalize rural communities, worked to improve public education and so much more. And now, he wants to take the fight to Washington.
On the other hand, his opponent Michael Whatley is an ex-Big Oil lobbyist who was handpicked by Donald Trump to push his agenda.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: This is their war.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
The GOP hasn’t lifted a finger to stop this war. They are all — almost every single one of them — falling in line behind Trump.
#

Third Battalion, 25th Marines, Fourth Marine Division. 3/25.
I was in Lima Company, and we went to Iraq in 2005.
14 of the 3/25 were killed in a single explosion, and 10 of them were from Lima.
We lost 48 guys in total on that deployment, and 23 of them were from Lima. They were my friends. We were the hardest hit Marine unit in the Iraq War.
So, when I see confirmed reports of Americans killed at war, it hits me a little differently than most people. I know what it’s like coming back to base with empty bunks. I know the toll it takes on your family. I know what it’s like to live with that experience after you come home. And I know better than most what it’s like fighting for your country in a war you don’t understand.
I also know this: Most people are afraid to talk about this. They don’t know how to talk about casualties, or even the military in general. They’re afraid to, because they don’t understand it. Not me.
The GOP hasn’t lifted a finger to stop this war. They are all — almost every single one of them — falling in line behind Trump. They are giving their consent to a war with no end in sight, and every American who comes home in a flag-draped coffin is because of them.
This is their war, and I am going to do everything in my power to make sure the American people never forget who’s to blame.
Help me beat these people. Help me hold them accountable. Help me win back majorities in the House and Senate so we can stop Trump from destroying this country and getting more Americans killed.

This race could be the one that decides the majority.

In a moment, I’m going to ask you to [**split a contribution between my campaign and James Talarico.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260309-2.o945Y5&refcode=em20260309-2925&t=2&akid=2925%2E21716%2E045t2M)
But first, I want to share why James gives me so much hope, and why his race is so important.
James is a Texas state representative, a former middle school teacher, and an eighth-generation Texan who has spent his time in office taking on the billionaire mega-donors and puppet politicians who’ve bought out Texas politics.
**He often says the biggest divide in our country isn’t left vs. right. It’s top vs. bottom.** It’s between the people with all the wealth and power — and everyone else working hard to build a good life for their families. That’s why he’s spent his career fighting against corruption and winning power back for working people.
Now James is running for the U.S. Senate with a message that feels rare in politics right now — one rooted not in fear, hate, or division, but in _**love**_ for our neighbors and country.
[**If you’re hungry to elect leaders like James Talarico to the Senate, will you split a donation of $5 between his campaign and mine today?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260309-2.o945Y5&refcode=em20260309-2925&amount=5&t=3&akid=2925%2E21716%2E045t2M)

**Democrats need to flip four seats to take back the U.S. Senate — and this race could be the one that decides the majority.**
Right now, polling shows the general election will start in a dead heat against either Ken Paxton or John Cornyn, who are headed into a runoff.
**Ken Paxton** was impeached by a bipartisan majority in the Texas House and is currently being called "unelectable" by members of his own party.
Meanwhile, **John Cornyn** is being propped up by super PACs. John and his allies spent _millions of dollars_ , yet still struggled to make it to the Republican runoff.
**But make no mistake: whoever emerges as the Republican nominee will have enormous outside spending behind them to keep Texas red.**
James has a rare window to build momentum while Republicans are tearing each other apart. And in a race that’s set to be a nail-biter, every dollar counts.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. Peter,

While the rise in popularity of politicians like Zohran Mamdani and his socialist policies might have come as a shock to many, I've been warning people about it for years.

Younger Americans do not know what socialism means.

When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark.

They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist.

**Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand.**

Rand wrote novels like _We The Living_ , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, _Atlas Shrugged_ , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement."

The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do.

That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events.

I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas.

Younger Americans do not know what socialism means. When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark. They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist. Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand. Rand wrote novels like We The Living , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, Atlas Shrugged , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement." The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do. That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events. I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas. Otherwise, please let me explain why I believe The Atlas Society and its leadership are best suited to combat the rise in popularity of these harmful ideologies. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240737%2E444211%2EEK2h16)
I’ve always thought of Powered by People as a startup. We have to be lean, we have to be fast, and most importantly, we have to be resilient.
That resilience was put to the test in 2025. Between the Texas Campus Protection Act designed to silence the students we work with and Ken Paxton’s office trying to shut us down, it was a tough year. We’ve spent nearly $400,000 in legal fees just fighting the Attorney General in courts from Tarrant County to the Texas Supreme Court.
To keep the lights on and stay in the fight, we had to make the hard call to significantly reduce our staff last year. For a while, we weren’t even sure what 2026 would look like.
**But we didn’t go away.** We decided to buckle up and ramp back up with a vengeance because we know our model works. **In 2024, the statewide turnout rate for the specific group of voters we worked with (18-29 year olds) was 79%, compared to just 37% for the rest of the state.**
I want to show you exactly what rebuilding looks like on the ground right now. When I look at our data (which I do daily because I am a data nerd!), I don’t just see numbers. I see the scale of a movement rebuilding at a level they never expected:
* **Our biggest week yet:** A few weeks ago, while Beto was visiting MSU, UNT, UTA, UTD, and TWU, we mobilized over 2,000 voters in just five days.
* **The 10k Milestone:** This past weekend, we officially surpassed 10,000 total voters mobilized year-to-date. That’s 10,000 Texans who now have a real person they can text when they have a question about voting.
* **The Momentum:** We reached 2,920 people in January. In February, we more than doubled that, reaching 7,081.
* **The Foundation:** These new contacts are joining a powerful network of nearly 50,000 voters already in our system from 2024 and 2025.

I’m proud of that 10k mark, but I’m also a realist. To win this year, our target is to mobilize **100,000 voters** before the midterms.
The math is simple. 10,000 in two months is a strong start, but it isn’t enough to get us to the finish line. We have to scale, and we have to do it fast. This isn’t just about registering voters and moving on; it’s about building the human relationships that ensure those voters actually make it to the polls.
We are leaving it all on the field this year. We need volunteers to have these conversations, and we need the resources to support our student leaders on campuses across the state.
[**Will you pitch in $3 today to help our organizers, volunteers, and student leaders reach our 100,000 voter goal?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260309.1Rfvg1&refcode=ema20260309-240737&t=3&akid=240737%2E444211%2EEK2h16)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260309.1Rfvg1&refcode=ema20260309-240737&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=240737%2E444211%2EEK2h16)**
See you out there,
Aimee Prudhomme
Executive Director, Powered by People

[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pbp-em-2023-footer?refcode=em20260309-240737-footer&t=23&refcode2=240737_444211_EK2h16&akid=240737%2E444211%2EEK2h16)

I came to this country alone at 16 years old – scared, far from home, and unsure what my future would hold.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260309-5988-footer&t=1&akid=5988%2E420207%2EJ4_j1H)
Hi Peter, Pramila Jayapal here.

[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260309.Htp13e&refcode=em20260309-5988&t=2&akid=5988%2E420207%2EJ4_j1H)
I came to this country alone at 16 years old – scared, far from home, and unsure what my future would hold.
I got the chance to live my American dream, becoming an organizer, an immigrant rights advocate, and eventually a member of Congress fighting for working people.
Now, it’s sickening to see politicians backed by billionaires try to slam the door shut on aspiring Americans — even unleashing masked ICE agents to terrorize and detain our neighbors.
**This isn’t just politics for me. It’s personal.**
And it’s why we’re building a people-powered movement to fight back against ICE’s cruelty and ensure that EVERY person who calls this country home is treated with dignity.
I don’t take corporate PAC money, and I don’t seek out billionaires to use as ATMs. This campaign runs on grassroots supporters like you, pitching in a few bucks at a time. So far this year, our average online contribution is just $26.20.
[**So Peter, if you believe everyone deserves the same chance I had, will you chip in what you can today to help us keep building this movement?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260309.Htp13e&refcode=em20260309-5988&t=3&akid=5988%2E420207%2EJ4_j1H)

Peter, You may have seen some of the Tweets my opponent has posted over the last few days. If you haven’t, here is just one of the many posts: [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/xxS4jO9mSc3SYFin3NOzWg~~/AAUS1hA~/bYNg2LrSboIYWQu-dovGbRzMMyONGPB571sjxrpMAJYGq_cyMUE41UNkqtvj78a47nNhkO97BHrywRCgqmRH0mcCSrsV_axNuPXPfok7J9WVk5saOcZrjuIV_VZQ0lW-KsUHGQdI5zH5IDpy05CP_2s_okmC9T63bRnRtuoW5I6qO_rP1zr-P_cGqfSKXecI922yIkQl08o3lau9ClFHl0zEUobhlhVNwuopxM42544XuIx7MG-1nSh-1o5oSJXy) I’ll be honest with you: it’s disappointing and embarrassing.

At a time when families across TN-5 are worried about skyrocketing gas prices, the last thing people need from their representative is more divisions and political theater. The truth is, this kind of rhetoric is a distraction. Just two weeks ago, my opponent was bragging about low gas prices. Now gas prices are at record highs, and families across Tennessee are feeling it every time they pull up to the pump. Rural hospitals are struggling. Health care costs keep rising. And too many working families are trying to stretch every dollar as far as possible. Those are the issues our leaders should be focused on. As mayor, I’ve always believed leadership means focusing on the things that actually impact people’s lives — fixing problems, bringing people together, and doing the work that actually helps communities move forward.

That’s the kind of leadership I will bring to Congress. If you believe TN-5 deserves leadership that is focused on real issues, not spectacle, I hope you’ll stand with this campaign.

body:
https://alexkelloff.com/ [https://alexkelloff.com/]
A Letter from Alex
I’m not running for Congress because someone encouraged me to jump in at the last minute. Running for Congress is a full-time job - and I don’t show up to work late.
For the past 10 months, I’ve been on the road across Colorado’s 3rd District because I care deeply about the people and communities here. I’ve visited all 27 counties, driven thousands of miles, and held over 100 events. And more than 2,300 grassroots supporters have already stepped up to support this campaign.
Work ethic is something I learned early in life. My father is 82 years old and still shows up to work for the Federal government every day - and that’s the same work ethic I’ll bring to Congress, fighting for this district every single day.
My family’s roots in this district go back more than 130 years, when my great-grandfather and his brothers immigrated to Trinidad, CO in 1893. This district isn’t just where I’m running - it’s home and the values I was raised on.
Everywhere I go, I hear the same concerns from people across the district. Folks are worried about losing the healthcare they depend on , struggling to find jobs that pay enough to live where they work , and wondering whether homeownership has become a luxury instead of the American dream.
If elected, my focus will be on:
* Creating good-paying jobs
* Lowering the cost of living
* Protecting our public lands and water
* Upholding the rule of law
But winning in CD-3 isn’t a one-person job. To succeed, you need a great team - and I’m proud of the team we’re building.
I’m honored to have the support of leaders from across the district, including former Congressman John Salazar, Arnold Salazar, former CD-3 candidates Sol Sandoval, Gail Schwartz, and Diane Mitsch Bush, State Senator Roberts, State Representatives Velasco, Martinez, Lukens, Stewart, and Mauro, Rocky Ford Mayor Duane Gurule , and former Grand Junction mayors Ana Stout, Chuck McDaniel, Ann Landman, and Blanca O’Leary, among many others.
You don’t win 27 counties without a lot of elbow grease - and we’ve done the work.
I truly believe we have the right campaign, the right message, and the right moment to flip this seat blue in November.
I look forward to seeing many of you on the campaign trail in the next couple of weeks.
Juntos podemos.
— Alex
February Recap:
February was once again a busy and productive month for our campaign as we planned and organized a full schedule of events, travel, and outreach for the spring and summer ahead. With a strong roadmap in place, we’re focused on showing up everywhere in the district and building the coalition we need to win.
Throughout the month, Alex traveled across Colorado’s 3rd District - meeting with community members, local leaders, and small business owners to hear directly about the challenges people are facing and the opportunities ahead.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak?]
Our campaign has now held more than 100 events across the district and raised over $1 million from more than 2,300 individuals, a testament to the growing momentum behind this campaign and the broad coalition we are building to win in November. Below is a map highlighting some of the communities we’ve visited over the past 10 months as we continue traveling across Colorado’s 3rd District to listen, learn, and earn the support of voters.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak?]
Holding Hurd Accountable
Trump Unendorses Hurd: Jeff Hurd just learned a hard lesson: you can’t buy loyalty in Washington. He spent months being a partisan rubber stamp - doing things like voting in favor of The One Big Beautiful Bill, which harms our rural hospitals, or waiting for Trump’s approval to vote for the release of the Epstein files.
This is what happens when you prioritize party games over the people who actually elected you. By contrast, I’m the only candidate in this race who isn't waiting for a text message from Washington to tell me how to vote. Let’s get back to focusing on Colorado, putting our people above political maneuvering.
Hurd Votes No on the Iran War Powers Resolution: Jeff Hurd’s vote against the Iran War Powers Resolution and the failure of the resolution to pass are prime examples of Congress forfeiting its constitutional duty.
As the Iran War continues, the cost of this conflict is no longer theoretical. Seven American service members have died as of the time of writing this, and with insiders saying the war may last until September, this toll will rise. This is a war of choice, launched without the consent or desire of the American people. Yet, when given the chance to demand oversight and stop this reckless escalation, Jeff Hurd chose to remain complicit in this illegal action.
The price of this war will not only be measured in lives lost, but also in the continuing increase in the cost of living, which will especially impact those who can least afford it as they face increased costs and soaring gas prices. As the global economy descends into turmoil, we cannot allow this unauthorized escalation to spiral into a global catastrophe while Jeff Hurd stands by and does nothing.
What’s Coming Soon
The next few weeks are packed with opportunities to connect with folks across the district. Stay tuned for specific times and locations. We are continuing to add new events across the district to learn and listen. Stay tuned for specific times and locations - and be sure to check our emails and social media accounts as new events are added. We look forward to seeing you on the trail!
* March 10 - Pitkin County Assembly
* March 14 - Pueblo County Assembly
* March 19 - Jonathan Godes BOCC Campaign Launch Party in New Castle
* March 22 - Beaver Creek Fundraiser
* March 27 - Gunnison Meet and Greet
* March 28 - Colorado Democratic Party State Assembly in Pueblo
* March 28 - No Kings Pueblo
* March 29 - Alamosa Meet and Greet
* April 2 - Grand Junction Fundraiser
* April 18 - Huerfano County Mother Jones Dinner
* April 25 - Grand Junction Fundraiser
You’ll also be hearing Alex’s voice on the airwaves. Throughout March and April, Alex is joining several podcasts and radio shows to talk about the race and the issues that matter most to Southern and Western Colorado. Alex was on the Gondolacast [https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-gondolacast-037-alex-kelloff-for-co/id1495925133?i=1000748856900] , Kate for the People [https://substack.com/home/post/p-185548997] , the Bill & Jeff [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GRuQXI5eT6U] radio show, the San Luis Valley Voices [https://slvoices.com/podcasts/] podcast, and the Gaze at the Parks [https://open.spotify.com/show/01PZ6PCsUuTU69rVInbYF2] podcast in February, with an appearance on the Blue-Lusional podcast scheduled for March 11th.
In addition to these events, we’ll be hosting fundraisers and continuing our tour of public events all across the district - showing up, listening, and making sure every community has a voice.
If you’d like to host a Meet & Greet to meet Alex, ask questions, and share your thoughts, please email campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] and a member of our team will follow up quickly to discuss scheduling. We’d also be happy to schedule a virtual meet and greet.
We’d love to hear from you — it’s incredibly important that Alex hears from the people he hopes to represent.
What You Can Do

FOLLOW ON SOCIAL MEDIA: Stay up to date with my team at Facebook, [https://www.facebook.com/alexkelloffco/] X [https://x.com/alexkelloffco] , Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/alexkelloffco/] , TikTok [https://www.tiktok.com/@alexkelloffco] , Bluesky [http://bsky.app/profile/alexkelloffco.bsky.social] and Substack [https://substack.com/@alexkelloffco?]

3. FINANCIALLY SUPPORT: Donate to my campaign today » [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak]

4. HOST A MEET & GREET: Contact campaign@alexkelloff.com [campaign@alexkelloff.com] , and we'll quickly follow up with you to discuss hosting an event.

Hi Peter, it’s Ken Burns.
I’ve dedicated my life to telling America’s stories through film. Oftentimes, these stories aren’t easy. They examine moments of our country in crisis and threats to our democracy.
What I’ve learned is this: Democracy is a fragile, imperfect project. It works when people with different backgrounds, ideas, and values can come together to agree on a vision for the future.
But this spirit of democracy is under a brutal assault.
Rule of law. Constitutionally protected rights. Dissent and freedom.
The best chance we have to protect these rights is at the ballot box.
_As citizens, it’s the test of our lifetimes._
And Jon Ossoff’s Senate race in Georgia will be one of the most important elections in the midterms.
Georgia could decide the Senate majority. Jon is the GOP’s top target this year and they’ll resort to every trick in the book to try to defeat him.
**[History will remember our actions at this moment. That’s why I’m standing with Jon Ossoff — and I’m asking you to join me. Can you chip in $5, or whatever you’re able to give, to Jon’s campaign today?**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-mar26.B6mAX1&refcode=em260309-1-f&t=2&akid=1808%2E5691347%2Exl4IR2)

I hope I can count on you to join me in supporting Jon Ossoff today. Our democracy depends on it.
Thank you.
Ken
